items.title: The coinvariant algebra of a finite Weyl group
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the cited invariant-theory results
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with
Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ and Weyl group $W$, acting on $\mathfrak h^*$
by the root reflections of [[def-root-reflections-and-the-weyl-group-action]]
([[def-finite-weyl-root-system-lattice-and-chamber-conventions]]), hence on the
symmetric algebra $S=S(\mathfrak h^*)$ by graded algebra automorphisms; a nondegenerate $W$-invariant bilinear form identifies $\mathfrak h$
with $\mathfrak h^*$ and thus identifies $S$ with $S(\mathfrak h)$ as
a graded $W$-algebra. Such a form is the complexification of a positive
definite form on the real Cartan, obtained by averaging any positive
definite form over finite $W$. Fix this identification; the page writes
$S=S(\mathfrak h)$ for either presentation. Write
$$S^W_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}(S^W)_d,\qquad I:=S\,S^W_+,$$
so that $I$ is the homogeneous ideal of $S$ generated by the invariants of
positive degree; this is the specialization to the reflection group case of
the quotient construction of
[[def-finite-linear-invariant-and-coinvariant-polynomial-algebras]], because
$S^W_+$ is exactly the space of positive-degree elements of the invariant
algebra $S^W$.

The **coinvariant algebra** of the pair $(\mathfrak h,W)$ is the graded
quotient
$$C=C(\mathfrak h,W):=S/I.$$
It is a commutative graded $\mathbb C$-algebra with $C_0=\mathbb C$: the ideal
$I$ is homogeneous of positive degree, so constants survive and every
homogeneous piece of $S$ maps onto its image. The quotient map
$$\rho:S\longrightarrow C,\qquad \rho(f)=f+I,$$
is a surjective graded algebra homomorphism, and the action of $W$ on $S$
descends to a $\mathbb C$-linear action on $C$ by graded algebra
automorphisms, because $I$ is $W$-stable. The algebra $C$ is finite
dimensional: $W$ is generated by its root reflections, so
[[thm-chevalley-shephard-todd-for-finite-weyl-groups]] writes $S$ as a free
module of finite rank over the polynomial algebra $S^W$, and
[[lem-weyl-coinvariant-hilbert-series-has-order-w-dimension]] gives
$\dim_{\mathbb C}C=|W|<\infty$ with the graded Hilbert series recorded there.

**Degree normalization.** Throughout the Soergel material on this page the
Cartan generators are given degree $2$, that is $\deg\mathfrak h=2$; the
symmetric algebra $S$ is then graded with $\deg S_d=2d$ for homogeneous
polynomials of ordinary degree $d$, and $C$ inherits this doubled grading. In
particular a basic invariant of ordinary degree $d_i$ has page degree $2d_i$,
and the top nonzero degree of $C$ is $2N$ with
$N=\sum_i(d_i-1)$. The separate degree-sum lemma on this page proves
that this number equals the positive-root count.

**Auxiliary permutation model for type $A$.** For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_n$
one may instead work with the place-permuting $S_n$-action on the auxiliary
polynomial ring $S_{\mathrm{perm}}=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, where a
permutation $\sigma$ sends $x_i$ to $x_{\sigma(i)}$, and with the quotient
$$C_{\mathrm{perm}}:=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(e_1,\dots,e_n),$$
where $e_1,\dots,e_n$ are the elementary symmetric polynomials. Splitting the
permutation representation $\mathbb C^n=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathbb C\cdot(1,\dots,1)$
into its sum-zero Cartan part and its fixed average coordinate exhibits
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_n]\cong S(\mathfrak h)\otimes\mathbb C[e_1]$ with
$e_1=x_1+\cdots+x_n$ the invariant coordinate, and restriction to the hyperplane
$e_1=0$ has kernel $(e_1)$. By [[thm-fundamental-theorem-of-symmetric-polynomials]], $e_1,\dots,e_n$
generate the invariant algebra and its positive-degree ideal of the permutation action, while $e_2,\dots,e_n$ restrict to basic
invariants of $S(\mathfrak h)^W$, dividing out by the positive-degree invariants
commutes with this presentation and yields a canonical isomorphism of graded
algebras
$$C(\mathfrak h,W)\cong C_{\mathrm{perm}}=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(e_1,\dots,e_n),$$
in which $x_i$ has degree $2$ and $e_i$ has degree $2i$. Elements of $C$ are
written as classes $\rho(f)$; the auxiliary model is used only for explicit
rank computations and never replaces the intrinsic definition.

The quotient and finite coordinate constructions require no additional choice;
the freeness and Hilbert-series conclusions inherit AC from their suppliers.
items.strategy: The published definition is quoted for a finite linear group and specialized to the reflection group case; the quotient by the ideal generated by positive-degree invariants is the same construction because $S^W_+$ is the space of invariants of positive degree. Degree normalization is a convention fixed here once for the whole page; For sl_n, split the permutation representation into its sum-zero Cartan and its fixed average coordinate. The fixed coordinate is the invariant e_1/n and is killed in the coinvariant quotient; therefore the auxiliary n-variable quotient by e_1,...,e_n is the Cartan coinvariant algebra, although the unreduced permutation polynomial ring has one extra variable. Products of factors use the corresponding tensor product.

items.title: The regular integral block and its antidominant weight
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory
([[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]],
[[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Work in category $\mathcal O$ of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie
algebra $\mathfrak g$ with the conventions of [[def-bgg-category-o]]: a Cartan
subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, a positive system with simple roots $\alpha_i$, the
Weyl group $W$ of [[def-root-reflections-and-the-weyl-group-action]], the Weyl
vector $\rho$, and the dot action $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$. Write
$Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$ and $\mu\le\lambda$ when
$\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$.

**The fixed weight.** Fix a weight $\lambda$ which is **integral**,
**dot-regular** and **dominant**: $\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z$
for every root $\alpha$ (so the integral Weyl group $W_\lambda$ of
[[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]] is all of $W$), and
$\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\neq0$, respectively $>0$, for every
root, respectively every positive root ([[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]]).
The set $\Phi_\lambda$ of [[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]] is therefore
the full root system and $W_\lambda=W$.

**The block.** The regular point $\lambda+\rho$ lies in an open chamber. An element fixing
it preserves that chamber, so [[thm-the-weyl-group-acts-simply-transitively-on-weyl-chambers]]
makes its stabilizer trivial; hence the linkage class
$$C=W_\lambda\cdot\lambda=W\cdot\lambda$$
has exactly $|W|$ elements. The **regular integral block** is the full
subcategory
$$\mathcal O_\lambda:=\mathcal O_C$$
of objects of $\mathcal O$ whose simple composition factors have labels in
$C$, as in [[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]]; it is
nonzero, abelian and extension-closed as a block, and
$K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$ is the subgroup of $K_0(\mathcal O)$ of
[[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]] spanned by the classes
of objects of the block.

**Its labelled objects.** For $w\in W$ define the standard and costandard
objects and the simple object by
$$\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):=M(w\cdot\lambda),\qquad \nabla(w\cdot\lambda):=D(M(w\cdot\lambda)),\qquad L(w\cdot\lambda):=M(w\cdot\lambda)/J(w\cdot\lambda),$$
where $M$ is the Verma module of [[def-verma-module]], $D$ the restricted dual
of [[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], and $J(w\cdot\lambda)$
the sum of all proper submodules, so that $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ is the unique
simple quotient of $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ by
[[thm-verma-module-has-a-unique-simple-quotient]]. By
[[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]] the simple
objects of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ are exactly the $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ for
$w\in W$, pairwise non-isomorphic. Let $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ denote a projective
cover of $L(w\cdot\lambda)$, which may be chosen inside the linkage class of
$w\cdot\lambda$ and is unique up to isomorphism and indecomposable
([[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]); every such $P(w\cdot\lambda)$
carries a finite Verma flag
([[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]],
[[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]).

**Triangularity of the Verma-flag matrix.** For all $v,w\in W$,
$$[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(v\cdot\lambda)]\neq0\ \Longrightarrow\ v\cdot\lambda\le w\cdot\lambda,\qquad [\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]=1,$$
where the multiplicity is the composition multiplicity of
[[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]]. Indeed
$(P(v\cdot\lambda):\Delta(w\cdot\lambda))=[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(v\cdot\lambda)]$
by [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]] and
$(P(v\cdot\lambda):\Delta(w\cdot\lambda))\neq0$ forces
$w\cdot\lambda-v\cdot\lambda\in Q^+$ while
$(P(v\cdot\lambda):\Delta(v\cdot\lambda))=1$ by
[[cor-projective-standard-labels-lie-above-the-head]].

**The antidominant weight.** Let $w_0\in W$ be the longest element. Since
$\langle w_0\cdot\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle
=\langle\lambda+\rho,w_0^{-1}\alpha^\vee\rangle<0$ for every positive root
$\alpha$, the antidominant Verma module $\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ is simple
([[cor-antidominant-verma-modules-are-simple]]), so
$$\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$$
and this is the unique standard object of the block that is simple: for
$w\neq w_0$ the regular weight $w\cdot\lambda$ is not antidominant, so some
positive root $\alpha$ has
$\langle w\cdot\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$, and
[[thm-verma-embedding-for-an-arbitrary-positive-root]] embeds
$M(s_\alpha\cdot(w\cdot\lambda))$ as a proper submodule of
$\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$. The weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$ is called the
**antidominant weight** of the block and $\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ its
antidominant Verma module.

**Grothendieck group.** By [[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]]
applied to the finite label set $C=W\cdot\lambda$, both the classes
$[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]$ and the classes $[L(w\cdot\lambda)]$, $w\in W$,
form $\mathbb Z$-bases of $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$, and the transition matrix
between them is unitriangular for any linear order of $W$ extending the order
on the dot orbit induced by $\le$.

Every statement above uses the published block, Verma, duality and
projective-cover theory named in the citations, and that theory assumes the
Axiom of Choice; the definition itself selects nothing further.
items.strategy: The block decomposition, linkage classes and the description of central characters are the published items; integrality identifies the integral Weyl group with $W$ and hence the linkage class with the $|W|$-element dot orbit; regularity of $\lambda$ makes its dot-action stabilizer trivial used by the published translation-functor definitions. Indexing of simples and Vermas, the triangularity of the Verma-flag matrix ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]] with [[cor-projective-standard-labels-lie-above-the-head]], read in the direction $[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(v\cdot\lambda)]\neq0\Rightarrow v\cdot\lambda\le w\cdot\lambda$) and the Grothendieck-group bases are the published facts. Every regular integral block has a unique dominant representative in its dot orbit, and that representative is used throughout.

items.title: The sum of basic Weyl invariant degrees minus one counts positive roots
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from invariant theory. Let $\Phi$ be a
finite reduced crystallographic root system of rank $r$ in the real Cartan
space $E$ with Weyl group $W$
([[def-finite-weyl-root-system-lattice-and-chamber-conventions]],
[[def-root-reflections-and-the-weyl-group-action]]), and let
$S=\mathbb C[E]$ carry the induced graded $W$-action with Cartan generators in
ordinary degree $1$. Let $d_1,\dots,d_r$ be the ordinary degrees of basic
invariants, so that $S^W=\mathbb C[w_1,\dots,w_r]$ with $w_i$ homogeneous of
degree $d_i$ ([[thm-chevalley-shephard-todd-for-finite-weyl-groups]]). Then
$$\sum_{i=1}^r(d_i-1)=|\Phi^+|.$$
With the page degree normalization $\deg E=2$ the coinvariant algebra
$S/(S^W_+S)$ has top degree $2\sum_i(d_i-1)=2|\Phi^+|=|\Phi|$.
items.strategy: Use the Molien trace identity, proved by averaging each finite symmetric power: product_i(1-t^{d_i})^{-1}=|W|^{-1}sum_w det(1-tw)^{-1}. Put u=1-t. The invariant Hilbert product is (product_i d_i)^{-1}u^{-r}[1+(sum_i(d_i-1)/2)u+O(u^2)]. The identity term on the right is |W|^{-1}u^{-r}; the terms with codimension-one fixed space each have eigenvalue -1 on its orthogonal complement, hence contribute (2|W|)^{-1}u^{-(r-1)}+O(u^{-(r-2)}). Every other term is lower order. A codimension-one fixed-space element is a root reflection: its fixed hyperplane cannot contain a root-regular point, since chamber stabilizers are trivial; hence that hyperplane is one of the finitely many root hyperplanes. There is one reflection for each positive root. The known product_i d_i=|W| and comparison of the next Laurent coefficient prove the formula. Rank zero gives empty sums; rank one has just identity/reflection and the same expansion. No degree table or unproved exponent identity is used.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Representations of Lie Groups, MIT18.757 full lecture notes (2023)
references.locator: Section 17.4, Exercise 17.5(i): the ordinary-degree identity; expanded here by the next Laurent coefficient of the Molien trace formula, using the published coinvariant Hilbert computation

items.title: Adjoint isotypic modules have the zero-weight rank
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra, $S=S(\mathfrak g)$ the symmetric algebra of the adjoint
representation, $R=S^{\mathfrak g}$ its invariants, $Z=Z(U(\mathfrak g))$ the
center of the enveloping algebra, and let $\mathcal H\subseteq S$ be a Kostant
harmonic subspace, so that multiplication is an isomorphism
$R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathcal H\to S$ of graded $\mathfrak g$-modules with $R$
acting trivially ([[thm-kostant-harmonic-decomposition-of-the-symmetric-algebra]]).

For every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $E$ with zero-weight space
$E_0$, the module $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S)$ is a free graded
$R$-module of rank $\dim E_0$, and the module
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,U(\mathfrak g))$ is a free $Z$-module of
rank $\dim E_0$; with the filtered lifting $U(\mathfrak g)=Z\cdot\operatorname{sym}(\mathcal H)$
of [[thm-enveloping-algebra-is-free-over-its-center]] these freenesses are
compatible with the natural quotient maps. More precisely,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S)\cong R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\mathcal H),\qquad \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,U(\mathfrak g))\cong Z\otimes_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\mathcal H),$$
where $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\mathcal H)$ is a finite-dimensional
graded vector space of dimension $\dim E_0$; consequently every central
reduction has adjoint $E$-multiplicity $\dim E_0$, and the natural map
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S)\otimes_R R/R_+\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S/(R_+S))$
is an isomorphism onto a space of dimension $\dim E_0$.
items.strategy: It suffices to treat simple E and then direct sums. The harmonic decomposition and complete reducibility in each finite polynomial degree make Hom_g(E,Sg) a graded direct summand of a graded free invariant-ring module. A graded projective module bounded below with finite-dimensional graded pieces is graded free: choose homogeneous lifts of a basis modulo the positive invariant ideal, generate recursively by degree, split the resulting graded free surjection and use graded Nakayama on its kernel. Its basis multiplicity series H_E(q) has nonnegative coefficients, a priori possibly infinitely many. Character decomposition of Sym g and the polynomial invariant Hilbert series give sum_E H_E(q)chi_E=product_i[d_i]_q/product_{alpha in Phi}(1-q e^alpha). The Weyl character formula shows simple characters are orthonormal for the constant-term form (1/|W|)CT(phi psi* product_alpha(1-e^alpha)): substitute the alternating Weyl numerators; distinct dominant shifted orbits have zero constant cross term and each equal orbit has |W| terms. Hence H_E(q)=(product_i[d_i]_q/|W|)CT(chi_E* product_alpha(1-e^alpha)/(1-q e^alpha)). To justify the limit without an imported Haar argument, work on l2 of the full weight lattice, with shifts by roots. For a positive root alpha let U_alpha be the unitary shift and F_alpha(q)=(I-U_alpha)(I-qU_alpha)^{-1}. The norm-convergent geometric resolvent gives norm F_alpha<=2 and norm squared (F_alpha-I)delta_0=(1-q)/(1+q). The finitely many operators commute, so telescoping their product, moving the error factor to delta_0, proves F(q)delta_0->delta_0. For 0<=q<1 the constant term above is the inner product of this vector with its image under the finite Laurent-character shift operator; the negative-root factors are the adjoint positive-root factors. Geometric convergence and Cauchy-Schwarz justify the coefficient products. It tends to CT(chi_E*)=dim E_0. The prefactor tends to1 because product d_i=|W|. Nonnegative coefficients and this finite limit show the total number of homogeneous free generators is dim E_0, hence finite. Finally PBW symmetrization is g-equivariant; lifting the harmonic basis and the basic central symbols yields the filtered isomorphism Z tensor H->U by its associated graded isomorphism. Taking E-isotypics and then any central fiber proves the U and reduction assertions. This is the exact isotypic multiplicity statement, stronger than module freeness alone.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Representations of Lie Groups, MIT18.757 full lecture notes (2023)
references.locator: Section 13.1, Theorem 13.1 and its complete proof (printed pp. 71-73), and Section 13.5, Theorem 13.5 (printed p. 74): the isomorphism S(g) = S(g)^g tensor H and the isotypic multiplicity dim E_0 for the adjoint action, with the torus-limit replaced locally by the explicit finite root-lattice shift coefficient argument

items.title: Projective functors on a regular integral block
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory
([[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Fix a regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ as in
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]], with
inclusion $\operatorname{incl}_\lambda:\mathcal O_\lambda\to\mathcal O$ and
exact projection $\operatorname{pr}_\lambda:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_\lambda$
of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], so that
$\operatorname{pr}_\lambda\circ\operatorname{incl}_\lambda=\operatorname{id}$;
the block is a direct summand of $\mathcal O$ and contains the projective
covers $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ of [[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]. For a
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module $E$ define
the endofunctor
$$F_E:=\operatorname{pr}_\lambda\circ(E\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_\lambda\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\lambda .$$

**Basic properties.** The functor $F_E$ is well defined and additive:
$E\otimes-$ is an exact endofunctor of $\mathcal O$ and maps $\mathcal O$ into
itself ([[prop-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-category-o]]),
and $\operatorname{pr}_\lambda$ is exact. Hence $F_E$ is exact as a composite of
exact functors. It preserves projective objects: if $P\in\mathcal O_\lambda$ is
projective, then $E\otimes P$ is projective in $\mathcal O$
([[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]]),
and $\operatorname{pr}_\lambda$ preserves projectives
([[lem-block-projection-preserves-projectives]]). The zero module $E=0$
gives the zero functor, and $E=\mathbb C$ the identity functor, since the
one-dimensional trivial module acts by the identity.

**Projective functors.** A **projective functor** on
$\mathcal O_\lambda$ is an endofunctor of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ isomorphic to a
direct summand of some $F_E$, $E$ finite dimensional and
$\mathfrak h$-semisimple. Write $\mathcal F_\lambda$ for the full subcategory
of the endofunctor category of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ whose objects are the
projective functors, with arbitrary natural transformations as morphisms; it is
additive with the pointwise biproducts of [[def-additive-category]], and
"direct summand" means natural maps $i:F\to F_E$, $p:F_E\to F$ with $pi=1_F$;
then $ip$ is an idempotent natural transformation.

**Closure properties.** The class of projective functors is closed under
finite direct sums, composition, direct summands and passage to adjoints:

1. $F_{E\oplus E'}\cong F_E\oplus F_{E'}$, since tensoring with a direct sum
distributes over direct sums and $\operatorname{pr}_\lambda$ is additive.
2. $F_E\circ F_{E'}$ is a natural direct summand of $F_{E\otimes E'}$:
the natural block decomposition of $E'\otimes X$ splits off its
$\lambda$-component before applying $E\otimes-$ and the final projection.
Its complementary blocks can return to $\mathcal O_\lambda$, so an
isomorphism with the entire $F_{E\otimes E'}$ is not asserted.
3. $F_{E^*}$ is both a left and a right adjoint of $F_E$: this is
[[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]] applied to
the two generalized central characters of the block, since
$F_{E^*}=\operatorname{pr}_\lambda\circ(E^*\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_\lambda$
is the translation functor $T_{\chi_\lambda,E^*,\chi_\lambda}$ and similarly for
$F_E$.
4. A direct summand of an exact additive functor is exact, and a direct summand
of a functor preserving projective objects again preserves projective objects:
apply the splitting to the image of each object. Hence every projective functor
is exact and preserves projective objects, and composition of summand splittings makes a composite of projective
functors a summand of the composite of their ambient tensor functors. Clause 2
therefore proves closure under composition; clause 1 proves closure under sums.
For an adjoint, take the mate of the summand idempotent under clause 3; the
triangle identities carry its square to itself, and its image is the
corresponding adjoint summand of $F_{E^*}$.

This is the definition of Bernstein-Gelfand [BGe, Section 3.1] and of
[Soe90, Section 1.2]; unlike the functors $T_\lambda^\mu$ of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], projective functors are not
required to come from a single finite-dimensional tensor functor, only from a
direct summand of one.
items.strategy: All closure properties are inherited from the published tensor and block-projection items: exactness and preservation of projective objects, additivity, and the adjunction for $E^*\otimes-$; direct summands of exact functors are exact after splitting, and the idempotent-completion convention for additive categories is [[def-additive-category]]. The composition identity is the associativity of the tensor product of finite-dimensional modules. No choice is used beyond the inherited AC of the block theory.

items.title: The coinvariant algebra is a complete intersection with one-dimensional socle
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published invariant-theory
items. Let $W$ act on the Cartan space $\mathfrak h$ by reflections and on
$S=S(\mathfrak h)$ by graded algebra automorphisms, with coinvariant algebra
$C=S/I$ as in [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]. Let
$w_1,\dots,w_r$ be homogeneous basic invariants of page degrees
$2d_1,\dots,2d_r$, where $d_1,\dots,d_r$ are the classical degrees
($\deg\mathfrak h=1$; for the Cartan of $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ they are
$2,3,\dots,n$), so that $S^W=\mathbb C[w_1,\dots,w_r]$
([[thm-chevalley-shephard-todd-for-finite-weyl-groups]]), and let
$\rho:S\to C$ be the quotient by the ideal $I=(w_1,\dots,w_r)$. Put
$N:=\sum_{i=1}^r(d_i-1)$. Then:

1. The sequence $w_1,\dots,w_r$ is a homogeneous $S$-regular sequence and $C$
is a complete intersection: $C=S/(w_1,\dots,w_r)$ with
$$\operatorname{Hilb}(C,t)=\frac{\prod_i(1-t^{2d_i})}{(1-t^2)^r}=\prod_i(1+t^2+\cdots+t^{2(d_i-1)}),$$
so that $\dim_{\mathbb C}C_{2N}=1$ and $C_j=0$ for $j>2N$.
2. The multiplication pairing $C_i\times C_{2N-i}\to C_{2N}\cong\mathbb C$ is
nondegenerate for every $i$, and consequently
$$\operatorname{soc}(C)=\{c\in C:C_+c=0\}=C_{2N}$$ is one dimensional.
3. Equivalently, $C$ is a graded Gorenstein algebra with one-dimensional socle
in the top degree $2N$.
items.strategy: The basic invariant regular sequence gives the Koszul free resolution of C and the displayed Hilbert series. Compute Tor_r^S(C,k) in two ways. Tensor the invariant Koszul resolution with k: all differentials vanish, so its top homology is the one-dimensional k in degree sum_i 2d_i. Tensor instead the Koszul resolution of k on the r degree-two polynomial variables with C: its top homology consists exactly of the elements killed by every variable, namely socle(C), shifted by 2r. The two Koszul calculations compute the same Tor (or use the finite free double Koszul complex and its two augmentations), so the socle is one-dimensional in degree 2sum_i(d_i-1)=2N. For nonzero homogeneous c, its nonzero ideal cC contains a nonzero element of maximal degree; multiplying that element by any positive variable is zero, hence it lies in this top socle. Thus c has a complementary-degree multiplier with nonzero product. This proves nondegeneracy of the top multiplication pairing on both sides; finite dimensions give perfectness. No dimension-symmetry shortcut or incorrect Ext-without-canonical-module shift is used.

items.title: The harmonic complement of the coinvariant algebra
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published invariant-theory
items. Let $W$ act on the Cartan space $\mathfrak h$ by reflections and on
$S=S(\mathfrak h)$ by graded algebra automorphisms, with coinvariant algebra
$C=S/I$ as in [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]. Then there
is a $W$-stable graded subspace $\mathcal H\subseteq S$, finite dimensional of
dimension $|W|$, such that the multiplication map
$$S^W\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathcal H\longrightarrow S,\qquad p\otimes h\mapsto ph,$$
is an isomorphism of graded $S^W$-modules and of $W$-modules, and the
restriction of the quotient map $\rho:S\to C$ to $\mathcal H$ is an isomorphism
of graded $W$-modules $\mathcal H\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }C$. One may take
$$\mathcal H=\{f\in S:\partial_pf=0\text{ for all }p\in S^W_+\},$$
using constant-coefficient differential operators from a $W$-invariant
positive definite form on $\mathfrak h_{\mathbb R}$. Any $W$-stable graded
complement of $I$ has the same multiplication and quotient properties. This
is the simultaneous kernel of all positive-degree invariant differential
operators, not in general the kernel of the quadratic Laplacian alone. In particular $\dim\mathcal H_d=\dim C_d$ for every $d$ and
$\sum_d\dim\mathcal H_d=|W|$.
items.strategy: Choose a positive definite $W$-invariant real form on $\mathfrak h$ (finiteness of $W$ allows averaging an arbitrary positive definite real form); extend it to a positive definite Hermitian form on each finite-dimensional graded piece $S_d$ for which the adjoint of multiplication is differentiation. Because $I$ and $S^W_+$ are $W$-stable and the form is $W$-invariant, the orthogonal complement $\mathcal H_d:=I_d^{\perp}$ is $W$-stable and $S_d=I_d\oplus\mathcal H_d$; hence $\mathcal H$ is a graded $W$-submodule and the restriction of $\rho$ is injective with image spanned by $\mathcal H$, giving $\mathcal H\cong C$ as graded $W$-modules. The isomorphism $S^W\otimes\mathcal H\to S$ follows by comparing graded ranks: $S$ is free of rank $|W|$ over $S^W$ by [[thm-chevalley-shephard-todd-for-finite-weyl-groups]], the map is $S^W$-linear and graded, and modulo $S^W_+$ it reduces to the isomorphism $\mathcal H\to C$ induced by $\rho$; graded Nakayama over the graded-local ring $S^W$ makes it surjective, and the rank count (both sides are free of rank $|W|$ over $S^W$) makes it injective. This is the reflection-group case of the harmonic-complement argument used on the published $S(\mathfrak g)$-page; only finite-dimensional linear algebra and the published freeness are used.

items.title: The deformed category O family over the Cartan symmetric algebra
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ be the symmetric algebra of
the Cartan subalgebra of [[def-bgg-category-o]], graded by $\deg\mathfrak h=2$
as fixed on this page ([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]],
[[def-multivariate-polynomial-ring-by-iteration]]). Let
$\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$ act on $S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda$
by
$$x\cdot(s\otimes1)=xs\otimes1+\lambda(x)s\otimes1\quad(x\in\mathfrak h),\qquad x\cdot(s\otimes1)=0\quad(x\in\mathfrak n^+),$$
where for $x\in\mathfrak h$, $xs$ means multiplication by the
linear polynomial $x\in S(\mathfrak h)$; $\mathfrak n^+$ acts trivially. Put
$$M_S(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}(S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda),$$
a module over $\mathfrak g\otimes S$: the left $\mathfrak g$-action is induced,
and $S$ acts on the right by multiplication on the last factor, which commutes
with $\mathfrak g$. Specializing at a closed point $\epsilon$ of
$\operatorname{Spec} S$ gives
$$M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S\mathbb C_\epsilon\cong M(\lambda+\epsilon),$$
the Verma module of [[def-verma-module]]; this is the universal family of
Verma modules with deformation parameter $\epsilon$.

**The family.** For a localization $T$ of $S$ put
$M_T(\lambda):=M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S T$, and let $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ be the
full subcategory of $\mathfrak g\otimes T$-modules that are direct summands of
a finite direct sum of modules $E\otimes M_T(\lambda)$ for finite-dimensional
$\mathfrak g$-modules $E$. Write $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ for
$R=S_{(0)}$, the localization of $S$ at the origin of
$\operatorname{Spec} S$. The **deformed family** is the assignment
$T\mapsto\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ together with the specialization functors
$-\otimes_T\mathbb C_\epsilon$ at the closed points $\epsilon$ of
$\operatorname{Spec} T$. By the tensor identity for finite-dimensional modules
and the Verma flags of tensor products
([[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]]) the
specializations have Verma constituents of highest weights
$\lambda+\nu+\epsilon$, where $\nu$ runs through the weights of the
finite-dimensional tensor factors, and they can meet several
central-character blocks, whose labels are the dot-Weyl orbits through these
highest weights ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]); a generic
parameter is generally nonintegral, and the distinct constituent labels have distinct central characters at the
generic parameter: an equality $\lambda+\gamma+\tau+\rho=w(\lambda+\gamma'+\tau+\rho)$
as affine functions of $\tau$ forces $w=1$ by comparing linear parts,
and then $\gamma=\gamma'$ ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]).

**Selected components.** For a regular dominant integral source $\lambda$ as in
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] and a
dot-dominant integral target $\nu$, so that $\nu+\rho$ lies in the closed
positive chamber, denote by $\mathcal D_R^{[\nu]}(\lambda)$ the component of
$\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ whose closed fiber at the origin lies in the selected
target block $\mathcal O_\nu$ of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]. Finite Verma flags of the
deformed tensor products and pairwise-unit resultants of their
central-character polynomials define this component by actual central
idempotents over $R$, obtained from [[thm-chinese-remainder-theorem-for-comaximal-ideals]].
Indeed choose a linear combination $z$ of central elements separating the
finitely many distinct special characters. On each deformed Verma factor,
$z$ acts by a polynomial $c_i(\tau)$ by
[[lem-harish-chandra-projection-computes-highest-weight-scalars]], and a flag
is annihilated by $\prod_i(z-c_i(\tau))$. Group these factors by their
constant values at the origin; differences from different groups are units
in $R$, so their product polynomials are comaximal in $R[X]$. CRT gives
mutually orthogonal polynomial projectors, whose images are the selected
components and whose sum is the identity. Other central-character components remain part of the full tensor
family; thus whole-family statements and selected-block statements are
distinguished.

**Weight structure.** Write $\tau:\mathfrak h\to T$ for the tautological linear map.
Modules in $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ carry a **deformed weight decomposition**
$X=\bigoplus_\xi X^\xi$, where
$$X^\xi=\{m:(h-\tau(h))m=\xi(h)m\text{ for every }h\in\mathfrak h\}.$$
These are eigenmodules for $h-\tau(h)$, not ordinary complex weight spaces
for $h$. They are finite projective, hence locally free of finite rank over $T$, as follows from the PBW model of Verma modules and the
flatness of the localization
([[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]]). The
conventions are those of [Soe90, Section 2.1]; no choice beyond the inherited
Axiom of Choice of the block theory is used.
items.strategy: The construction is the standard universal family of Verma modules with a formal deformation parameter; the twisted $\mathfrak b$-action makes the fiber at $\epsilon$ the Verma module of weight $\lambda+\epsilon$, the right $S$-action commutes with $\mathfrak g$, and direct summands of finite tensor products give the analogue of the projective functors of [[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]] over $T$. Weight spaces are locally free by the PBW model of Verma modules; no choice beyond the inherited AC of the block theory is used. Tensor products have finite Verma flags by the PBW tensor identity and the weight filtration of the finite-dimensional b-module E; the deformed flag factors are M_T(lambda+nu). Direct-summand flags over local R follow by canonical maximal-weight peeling: U(g)X^nu=Delta_R(nu) tensor_R X^nu for a maximal label, every idempotent preserves this submodule, its top-weight image is finite free, and induction applies to the quotient. For selected components choose a central element separating the finitely many special central characters of these factors; its grouped annihilating polynomials have pairwise-unit resultants and hence Chinese-remainder projectors in R[X], which become actual central projectors. Thus whole-family statements and selected-block statements are distinguished. The generic regular/nonintegral Verma assertion follows from the Shapovalov determinant factors; generic here means the generic point or parameters avoiding the countably many reducibility hyperplanes, not a Zariski-open set on which integrality persists.

items.title: The nilpotent central fiber is reduced and integral
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ and Weyl group $W$,
and let $p_1,\dots,p_r$ be homogeneous basic generators of $S(\mathfrak g)^{\mathfrak g}$
of degrees $d_1,\dots,d_r$, corresponding by Chevalley restriction to basic Weyl
invariants ([[thm-symmetric-invariants-restrict-to-weyl-invariants]],
[[thm-chevalley-shephard-todd-for-finite-weyl-groups]]). Put
$$A=S(\mathfrak g)/(p_1,\dots,p_r).$$ Then $A$ is a reduced integral domain of
dimension $\dim\mathfrak g-r=2|\Phi^+|$, with Hilbert series
$$\operatorname{Hilb}(A,t)=\prod_{i=1}^r\frac{1-t^{d_i}}{(1-t)^{\dim\mathfrak g}},$$
and for every central character $\chi:Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to\mathbb C$ the PBW
associated graded of $U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi$ is canonically
isomorphic to $A$.
items.strategy: For g=0, A=C and the assertions are immediate; below use the nonzero semisimple case. Invariant-ring freeness makes p_i a regular sequence, so A is a complete intersection with the displayed Hilbert series; polynomial rings and their regular-sequence quotients are Cohen-Macaulay locally. Construct the principal triple e=sum e_i, h=2rho^vee, f=sum c_i f_i where h=sum c_i h_i. The simple root triples and invertible Cartan matrix give [h,e]=2e,[h,f]=-2f,[e,f]=h. Complete reducibility restricts the adjoint module to a sum of sl2 strings. Since ad h has only even eigenvalues and zero space the r-dimensional Cartan, there are r strings L_{2m_j}; no trivial string exists because a Cartan vector commuting with all simple e_i is zero. Thus m_j>0, sum m_j=|Phi^+|, ker ad e has dimension r and lies in n_+, and g=[g,e] direct-sum ker ad f. Let z_f=ker ad f, with lowest-string coordinates y_j. The restrictions q_i(y)=p_i(e+y) are algebraically independent: compose root-unipotent polynomial exponentials and diagonal root-character torus maps, acting on e+z_f. Choose dim[g,e] basis directions with independent commutators with e; together with z_f the coordinate map has nonzero square Jacobian at the origin. It is dominant: a polynomial relation of least degree on its image, differentiated through the generically invertible Jacobian, would have all its lower-degree partial derivatives zero, hence be constant in characteristic zero. Invariance would transfer any relation among q_i to that dense image and then to the algebraically independent p_i. The action x->t Ad(t^{-rho^vee})x fixes e and gives y_j weight m_j+1, so q_i is weighted-homogeneous of degree d_i. Algebraic independence in r variables implies its Jacobian is not identically zero: the fraction field C(y) is finite separable over C(q), and differentiating the minimal polynomials expresses the dy_j in the span of dq_i. Its determinant has weighted degree sum d_i-sum(m_j+1)=0 by the degree-sum lemma. All weights are positive, so this determinant is a nonzero constant. Thus dp_i(e) are independent; this supplies the missing Kostant-slice deduction rather than assuming individual degrees match the exponents. For the underlying zero set, put G=Aut(g)^0, an affine algebraic group defined by bracket preservation, smooth by Cartier in characteristic zero, with Lie algebra Der(g)=ad g. The diagonal root-character torus H and N_+=exp(ad n_+) are closed connected algebraic subgroups (exponential/logarithm and BCH are finite polynomials in the positive-height nilpotent matrices). H N_+ is a Borel: its Lie algebra b is maximal solvable, since any negative-root component in a larger algebra, isolated by Cartan weight projectors, supplies a root sl2 with b. A nilpotent ad x exponentiates to a connected unipotent subgroup contained in a Borel; Borel conjugacy puts x in b, and its Cartan component must vanish because otherwise ad x has a nonzero root eigenvalue. Hence every nilpotent is conjugate into n_+. Conversely all p_i vanish on n_+ by the contracting root torus. If all p_i vanish, all invariant traces Tr((ad x)^k) vanish; Newton identities make ad x nilpotent. The zero set is therefore the image of G times n_+, hence irreducible (smooth connected group varieties are irreducible). It is the closure of the principal orbit: in positive-height grading ad e:n_{+,k}->n_{+,k+1} is onto by the sl2 strings, so successive exponentials exp(ad x_k) prescribe each higher-height coefficient of e, and the torus prescribes nonzero simple coefficients; the Borel orbit contains the dense subset of n_+ with all simple coefficients nonzero. The nonradical-ideal clause of the published affine Jacobian criterion makes A regular at e, since its local dimension is dim g-r. Invariance makes the dense principal orbit regular, so A is generically reduced. For any associated prime q of A, its localization has depth0; local Cohen-Macaulayness gives dimension0, hence q is minimal. Irreducibility leaves one minimal prime, whose generic localization is a field by generic regularity. The published associated-prime detection map injects A into this field, proving reducedness and the domain assertion. Finally the filtered harmonic Z-free decomposition of U gives gr(U/ker chi)=Sg/(p_i): the leading central generators are p_i and specialization of the filtered free harmonic basis has exactly the quotient Hilbert series, so the natural graded surjection is an isomorphism. This works componentwise for semisimple g, not only type A.

items.title: The wall-crossing functor and its unit and counit
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block and
translation theory ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]).

Fix the dominant regular integral representative $\lambda$ of a regular
integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$
([[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]]) and an
integral weight $\mu$ such that $\lambda+\rho$ is regular dominant and
$\mu+\rho$ is dominant with dot stabilizer exactly $\{1,s\}$ for a reflection
$s=s_\alpha$; this is the dominant-chamber version of single-wall translation
data, the published
[[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]] being stated with
antidominant representatives, and the dominant standard counts below are
proved through the norm-distance and extremal-weight bounds
([[lem-dominant-norm-distance-comparison]],
[[lem-weight-norm-bound-for-finite-dimensional-simple-modules]]) rather than
by applying that datum literally. Let $\nu$ be the unique dominant element of
the linear Weyl orbit of $\mu-\lambda$ and let
$E=L(\nu)$ be the finite-dimensional simple module of highest weight $\nu$, so
that $\mu-\lambda$ is an extremal weight of $E$; write
$E^{*}=L(-w_0\nu)$ for its dual
([[prop-highest-weight-of-the-dual-representation]]).

With $\chi_\lambda,\chi_\mu$ the generalized central characters and
$\operatorname{pr}$ the exact central projections of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], define the **onto-wall** and
**out-of-wall** translations
$$T_{\mathrm{on}}:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\mu}\circ(E\otimes-)\big|_{\mathcal O_{\chi_\lambda}},\qquad T_{\mathrm{out}}:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}\circ(E^{*}\otimes-)\big|_{\mathcal O_{\chi_\mu}},$$
and the **wall-crossing functor**
$$\theta_s:=T_{\mathrm{out}}\circ T_{\mathrm{on}}\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\lambda .$$

**Basic properties.** Both translations are exact, and $T_{\mathrm{out}}$ is
both a left and a right adjoint of $T_{\mathrm{on}}$
([[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]]); hence
$\theta_s$ is exact and, as a composite of restriction-of-scalars and central
block projection applied to tensoring by $E^{*}\otimes E$, it is a natural
direct summand of the endofunctor
$\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}\circ((E^{*}\otimes E)\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_{\chi_\lambda}$,
so it is a projective functor on $\mathcal O_\lambda$ in the sense of
[[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]]. On
standard objects the dominant-chamber counts are
$T_{\mathrm{on}}\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$ and the
two-factor flag $[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(w\cdot s\cdot\lambda)]$ for
$T_{\mathrm{out}}\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$, as follows directly from the tensor flag and the two norm bounds above.
Put $v=\lambda+\rho$, $u=\mu+\rho$. A retained onto-wall label satisfies
$wv+\gamma=xu$ with $|\gamma|\le|u-v|$. Thus
$|\gamma|=|v-w^{-1}xu|\ge|v-u|$; equality and regularity of $v$ give
$w^{-1}xu=u$, leaving the single label $w\cdot\mu$, with its extremal
weight of multiplicity one. For the return translation,
$wu+\delta=xv$ implies equality in $|u-w^{-1}xv|\ge|u-v|$, so
$w^{-1}xv\in\{v,sv\}$ and $x\in\{w,ws\}$, again with
extremal weights of multiplicity one. These calculations use the Verma
tensor flag of [[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]].

**Unit and counit.** The two tensor-block adjunctions supply natural
transformations
$$\eta\colon\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal O_\lambda}\longrightarrow\theta_s,\qquad\varepsilon\colon\theta_s\longrightarrow\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal O_\lambda},$$
where $\eta$ is the unit of the adjunction $T_{\mathrm{on}}\dashv T_{\mathrm{out}}$
and $\varepsilon$ the counit of the adjunction $T_{\mathrm{out}}\dashv T_{\mathrm{on}}$;
each satisfies the triangle identities with its companion counit or unit on
the wall category, and these identities are part of the data. The pair
$(\theta_s,\eta,\varepsilon)$ is determined by the choice of the
biadjunction maps, which are fixed once and for all.

**Independence of the auxiliary weight.** Up to natural equivalence the
functor $\theta_s$ depends only on the wall $s$ and the block
$\mathcal O_\lambda$, not on the chosen ambient weight $\mu$: this
well-definedness statement is discharged forward by
[[thm-indecomposable-projective-functors-are-indexed-by-the-weyl-group]],
which lifts the equality of the evaluations on standard objects to a natural
equivalence; it is recorded in `justified_by` and is not used to construct
$\theta_s$ or to generate objects.
items.strategy: Exactness and biadjunction follow from finite-dimensional tensor-Hom pairing and exact central block inclusion/projection. The singular block projection is a natural idempotent on E tensor -, so composing it with E* tensor - gives the asserted summand of a single tensor functor. The dominant-chamber standard counts are proved by the general dominant norm-distance and extremal-weight bound, not by applying the printed antidominant-only datum literally. Their two-factor class on the dominant Verma is Delta_e+Delta_s. BGG reciprocity and the one-dimensional simple-root lowered weight give P_s the same flag; hence theta_s Delta_e=P_s. The later proved projective-functor classification lifts equality of these evaluations to natural equivalence, proving wall-weight independence. This is a forward well-definedness discharge, declared in justified_by, not a circular prerequisite for chosen-wall construction or object generation.

items.title: The coinvariant algebra is the graded regular representation of W
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published invariant-theory
items. Let $W$ be a finite Weyl group with reflection representation
$\mathfrak h$, coinvariant algebra $C=S(\mathfrak h)/S(\mathfrak h)S^W_+$ and
classical basic degrees $d_1,\dots,d_r$ as in
[[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]] and
[[lem-the-coinvariant-algebra-is-a-gorenstein-algebra-with-one-dimensional-socle]].
Then:

1. $C\cong\mathbb C W$ as a $W$-module: the coinvariant algebra is isomorphic
to the regular representation of $W$.
2. The graded $W$-character of $C$ is
$$\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)(w)=\sum_{i\ge0}t^i\operatorname{tr}(w\mid C_i)=\prod_{i=1}^r(1-t^{2d_i})\cdot\det(1-t^2w\mid\mathfrak h^*)^{-1}\qquad(w\in W),$$
an identity of rational functions whose limit at $t=1$ is $|W|$ for $w=1$ and
$0$ for $w\neq1$.
3. Equivalently, $C$ is the graded lift of the regular representation: if
$\operatorname{mult}_E(C,t)$ denotes the graded multiplicity of the irreducible
$W$-module $E$, then the identity
$\sum_E\operatorname{mult}_E(C,t)\chi_E(w)=\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)(w)$
determines the graded multiplicities uniquely, with
$\operatorname{mult}_E(C,1)=\dim E$. The Hilbert-series specialization of (2)
at $w=1$ is $\prod_i(1+t^2+\cdots+t^{2(d_i-1)})$, the published coinvariant
Hilbert series in the page normalization $\deg\mathfrak h=2$.
items.strategy: By [[lem-the-harmonic-complement-of-the-coinvariant-algebra]] the quotient map restricts to an isomorphism $\mathcal H\cong C$ of graded $W$-modules with $S=S^W\otimes\mathcal H$, so $\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)=\operatorname{HTr}(\mathcal H,t)$ and, since $S^W$ contributes the scalar factor $\prod_i(1-t^{2d_i})^{-1}$ to the graded trace of $S$, the identities of the published Hilbert-series lemma give $\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)=\operatorname{HTr}(S,t)\cdot\prod_i(1-t^{2d_i})$ with $\operatorname{HTr}(S,t)(w)=\det(1-t^2w|\mathfrak h^*)^{-1}$ (Molien's formula, proved there). For (1): evaluate at $t\to1$. The numerator vanishes to order exactly $r$ and the denominator to order $\dim\mathfrak h^w$; for $w\neq1$ the reflection representation is faithful, so $\dim\mathfrak h^w\le\dim\mathfrak h-1=r-1$ and the numerator order exceeds the denominator order, giving limit $0$ for $w\neq1$; at $w=1$ the limit is $\prod_i d_i=|W|$ by the published dimension formula. A finite-dimensional $\mathbb C$-representation is determined up to isomorphism by its character, so $C\cong\mathbb C W$ as $W$-modules. Part (3) is the standard description of graded $W$-modules by their graded characters and Krull-Schmidt uniqueness for the semisimple category of finite-dimensional $W$-modules over $\mathbb C$. The computation is choice-free except for the inherited AC of the published Hilbert-series lemma.

items.title: The antidominant projective and the Soergel functor
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory
([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]]).

In the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ of
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] fix the
antidominant weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$ and let
$$P:=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$$ be a projective cover of $L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$
([[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]); it is unique up to isomorphism and
indecomposable ([[prop-projective-covers-in-o-are-indecomposable-and-unique]],
[[def-projective-object]]), and it is an injective object of
$\mathcal O_\lambda$. The **Soergel functor** is
$$V:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,-)\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow \operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)^{\mathrm{op}}\text{-}\mathbf{mod},\qquad M\longmapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,M),$$
with the left action of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)^{\mathrm{op}}$ on
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,M)$ induced by composition on the right of
the source: $a\cdot f=f\circ a$
([[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]]). Its
values on the standard objects and on the indecomposable projectives are
written $V\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):=V(\Delta(w\cdot\lambda))$ and
$VP(w\cdot\lambda):=V(P(w\cdot\lambda))$. The functor $V$ is exact, because
$P$ is projective, and hence left exact; the identity
$VP\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ with its regular module structure
is the Yoneda identification. Replacing the chosen projective cover $P$ by an
isomorphic one changes $V$ by a natural equivalence of functors compatible
with the endomorphism-ring identification, so the construction depends only
on the isomorphism class of $P$.

**Well-definedness: $P$ is injective.** We prove that $P$ is an injective
object of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ using only the listed suppliers, following the
argument of [Soe90, Sections 1.2 and 2.1] in its algebraic form. Put
$\eta:=-\rho$; then $W\cdot\eta=\{\eta\}$, because $w\cdot\eta=w(\eta+\rho)-\rho=-\rho$
for every $w$ ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). By
[[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]] the simple
objects are the $L(\mu)$ with $L(\mu)$ determined by $\mu$, and the composition
factors of $M(\eta)$ have highest weights in $W\cdot\eta\cap(\eta-Q^+)=\{\eta\}$;
hence $M(\eta)=L(\eta)$ is simple. By BGG reciprocity
([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]) applied to the single-label block, and the existence
of Verma flags for projectives ([[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]]),
the projective cover $P(\eta)$ has a Verma flag with the single factor
$\Delta(\eta)=M(\eta)=L(\eta)$, so $P(\eta)\cong L(\eta)$; the block
$\mathcal O_\eta$ has a single simple object, which is projective, hence is
semisimple by enough projectives ([[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]),
and therefore every object of $\mathcal O_\eta$, in particular $L(\eta)$, is
injective as well as projective in $\mathcal O_\eta$
([[def-injective-object]]). A projective object of a block is projective in
$\mathcal O$ ([[lem-block-projection-preserves-projectives]]), and an
injective object of a block is injective in $\mathcal O$ because the block
decomposition is a direct sum of abelian subcategories and the exact
projections restrict split exactness blockwise. Second, we identify a
projective-injective object
in the block $\mathcal O_\lambda$: let $E=L(\lambda+\rho)$ be the
finite-dimensional simple module of highest weight $\lambda+\rho$
([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]])
and set
$$Q:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}\bigl(E\otimes L(\eta)\bigr)\in\mathcal O_\lambda,$$
the exact central projection of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]].
Since $L(\eta)$ is projective and injective in $\mathcal O$, the tensor product
$E\otimes L(\eta)$ is projective and injective
([[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]]),
and its direct summand $Q$ is projective and injective in $\mathcal O$; the
general exact tensor-block biadjunction of
[[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]] gives the
same conclusion with all adjoints and, by
[[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]],
injectivity (equivalently, $Q$ is a direct summand of a projective-injective
object, and injectivity passes to summands). Third, we compute a
one-dimensional Hom space: since $M(a)$ with $a=w_0\cdot\lambda$ is simple by
the same top-weight argument as for $\eta$ (every other highest weight in
$W\cdot a$ lies strictly above $a$ in the root order), the tensor product
$E^{*}\otimes M(a)$ has a finite Verma flag whose factors are the
$\Delta(a+\nu)$ with $\nu$ running through the weights of the dual module
$E^{*}$, by
[[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]]; here
$E^{*}=L(-w_0(\lambda+\rho))$ ([[prop-highest-weight-of-the-dual-representation]]).
Projecting to the central character $\chi_\eta$ retains exactly the factors
with $a+\nu\in W\cdot\eta=\{\eta\}$, that is $\nu=-w_0(\lambda+\rho)$, the
highest weight of $E^{*}$ of multiplicity one, so
$$\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\eta}\bigl(E^{*}\otimes M(a)\bigr)=L(\eta).$$
The tensor-hom adjunction and the tensor-block adjunction now give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(Q,L(a))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(L(\eta),E^{*}\otimes M(a))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(L(\eta),L(\eta))\cong\mathbb C,$$
because every homomorphism from the block-$\eta$ simple lands in the
$\chi_\eta$-summand and $L(\eta)$ is simple. Choose the nonzero, hence
surjective, element $q:Q\to L(a)$ and lift it through the projective cover
$P(a)\to L(a)$ to a map $Q\to P(a)$; its image is a submodule of $P(a)$
surjecting onto the head $L(a)$, hence is all of $P(a)$ by essentiality of a
projective cover, so the lift is surjective and splits by projectivity of
$P(a)$. Therefore $P(a)$ is a direct summand of the injective object $Q$
([[def-injective-object]]), and direct summands of injective objects are
injective, so $P=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ is injective. This argument uses
[[thm-bgg-verma-homomorphism-criterion]] only through the standard embedding
criterion implicit in the top-weight computations, and it does not assume the
Endomorphismensatz.

**The once-each flag.** The tensor flag of $E\otimes M(-\rho)$ has labels
$-\rho+\gamma$ for weights $\gamma$ of $E=L(\lambda+\rho)$. Projection to
$\chi_\lambda$ keeps precisely $\gamma\in W(\lambda+\rho)$, each of
multiplicity one by [[lem-weight-norm-bound-for-finite-dimensional-simple-modules]].
Thus $Q$ has each $\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)$ once. Every such Verma contains
$M(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(a)$ by
[[lem-dominant-integral-dot-translates-embed-in-the-verma-module]]. BGG
reciprocity gives $(P(a):\Delta(x\cdot\lambda))\ge1$; the splitting
$Q=P(a)\oplus Q'$ and
[[lem-direct-summands-of-verma-filtered-objects-are-verma-filtered]] give the
opposite bound one. Hence all these multiplicities equal one, $Q'$ has
an empty flag and is zero, and $Q=P(a)$. Since $P(a)$ is projective,
$V$ is exact and $\dim VX=[X:L(a)]$ for finite-length $X$: on simples its
values are $\mathbb C$ at the head label and zero otherwise. Consequently
$\dim V\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)=1$ for every $x$. Every simple submodule of a
Verma is itself a simple Verma: its universal Verma map into that Verma is
injective. Thus the unique simple standard $L(a)$ is its only possible
socle label, and [[thm-verma-homomorphism-spaces-have-dimension-at-most-one]]
makes this socle a single copy of $L(a)$.
items.strategy:
Injectivity has the following algebraic proof using only published suppliers. Put $\eta=-ho$. Every simple in its central-character summand has highest weight in $W\cdot\eta=\{\eta\}$, by highest-weight classification and the central-character theorem. Thus $M(\eta)=L(\eta)$: its top weight has dimension one and its finite composition series has only this simple. BGG reciprocity and a Verma flag give $P(\eta)=L(\eta)$; enough projectives then makes this one-simple block semisimple, so $L(\eta)$ is also injective. Let $E=L(\lambda+ho)$ and set $Q=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}(E\otimes L(\eta))$. The general tensor-block exact biadjunction proved in [[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]] shows that $Q$ is projective and injective. Set $a=w_0\cdot\lambda=w_0(\lambda+ho)-ho$. The same central-orbit/top-weight argument makes the antidominant $M(a)$ simple (any other highest weight in its dot orbit is strictly above $a$). Tensoring $E^*\otimes M(a)$ has a Verma flag with factors $M(a+
u)$ indexed by weights $
u$ of $E^*$. Projection to $\chi_\eta$ retains only $a+
u=-ho$, namely $
u=-w_0(\lambda+ho)$, the highest weight of $E^*$ of multiplicity one. Hence that projection is $L(\eta)$, and adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,L(a))=\mathbb C$. Lift the surjection $Q	o L(a)$ through the projective cover $P(a)	o L(a)$; essentiality of the cover makes the lift surjective, and projectivity of $P(a)$ splits it. Thus $P(a)$ is a summand of the injective $Q$ and is injective. This proof does not assume the Endomorphismensatz. Projectivity also makes $V$ exact (and hence left exact); independence of the chosen cover and $VP=\operatorname{End}(P)$ follow directly by composition and projective-cover uniqueness. In fact $Q=P(a)$: its projected tensor Verma flag consists of every $\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)$ once, since the retained E-weights are exactly the distinct extremal weights $x(\lambda+ho)$, all of multiplicity one. The published Verma embedding criterion embeds the simple $\Delta(a)=L(a)$ in every standard in the block, so BGG reciprocity makes every standard multiplicity in $P(a)$ at least one. Since $P(a)$ is a summand of the once-each flag of $Q$, all these multiplicities are exactly one and the complementary summand has no flag factors, hence is zero.

items.title: Duflo–Joseph g-finite endomorphisms of every Verma module
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra and let $\mu$ be a highest weight. The action of
$U(\mathfrak g)$ on the Verma module $M(\mu)$ induces an algebra isomorphism
$$U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \bigl(\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu)\bigr)^{\operatorname{ad}\mathfrak g\text{-finite}},$$
where the target is the locally finite part of the endomorphism algebra for
the adjoint action $x\mapsto[x,-]$. In particular
$\operatorname{Ann}M(\mu)=U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu$. Moreover, for every
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $E$,
$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))=\dim E_0,$$
and the action identifies each finite adjoint isotypic multiplicity with that
dimension.
items.strategy: If g=0 then U=M=C and all assertions are immediate; below assume N>0. First expand the field dimension argument. A finite-length Verma has a simple submodule L(eta); the universal highest-weight map M(eta)->M(mu) is injective, hence factors through a simple only if M(eta)=L(eta). Thus it has a simple Verma submodule. For a simple Verma M, restricted duality identifies D M=M. Tensor adjunction and the standard/costandard Hom–Ext vanishing compute Hom(M,E tensor D M)=Hom(E* tensor M,D M), whose dimension is the number of its M-standard factors, dim E_0. For arbitrary M(mu), the same Hom is the kernel of finitely many simple-raising equations on the finite PBW weight space (E tensor M(mu))_mu. Their matrices are polynomial in mu, so dimension is at least its generic simple-Verma value dim E_0. Let M(eta) subset M(mu) be the simple Verma just found. Its embedding as a left U(n_-) module is right multiplication u->u p by a nonzero singular PBW element p in U(n_-). The quotient has filtered growth O(n^{N-1}), N=dim n_-, because its associated graded is a quotient of the polynomial ring by the nonzero leading element, whose Hilbert series is (1-t^d)/(1-t)^N. Tensoring a finite-dimensional module preserves this growth bound. Hence a map M(mu)->E tensor M(mu) must take M(eta) into E tensor M(eta), since otherwise the simple source embeds in a module of that smaller growth. Restriction to M(eta) is injective: a map killing it factors through the smaller-growth quotient into the free U(n_-)-module E tensor M(mu). Freeness follows from the Hopf tensor identity u tensor v -> sum u_(1)m_mu tensor u_(2)v, whose inverse uses the antipode. Any nonzero vector in that finite free module generates a free copy of the PBW domain and has growth n^N, impossible for such a quotient image. Restriction thus bounds the original Hom by dim E_0, proving equality. For action injectivity, let v be the highest vector of the simple Verma M(eta) inside M(mu). Its Shapovalov pairing U(n_+)_beta times U(n_-)_(-beta)->C is perfect in every weight. In a nonzero x=sum_beta x_beta in U(n_-) tensor U(n_+), choose a minimal beta with x_beta=sum_i b_i tensor a_i nonzero and act on a dual PBW vector a_j^*v. All other terms vanish by highest-weight support and minimality; the result is b_j v, nonzero for some j. Therefore multiplication followed by action injects this 2N-dimensional PBW-growth space into the image of the central reduction. If the action kernel in U_chi were nonzero, its nonzero homogeneous graded ideal in the proved domain A would contain a principal nonzero homogeneous ideal A f. Multiplication by f is injective, and the complete-intersection Hilbert series shows the cumulative growth of A/(f) is O(n^{2N-1}), whereas the injected PBW subspace has growth bounded below by a positive multiple of n^{2N}. This contradiction proves action injectivity. Finally its E-isotypic source has dimension dim E_0 by the adjoint multiplicity lemma and its target has the same dimension by the field Hom calculation. The injective map is therefore onto each isotypic, and local finiteness/complete reducibility of the adjoint action gives the full algebra isomorphism. No unproved annihilator equality, nilpotent-cone reducedness or arbitrary-weight generic inference is used. For the generic kernel lower bound, simple-Verma weights are Zariski dense: a proper submodule has a minimal-positive-height singular vector of weight mu-beta. Equal quadratic Casimir scalars give 2(mu+rho,beta)=(beta,beta), impossible throughout the real negative chamber. This real open set is Zariski dense, and meets the maximal-rank open locus of the finite polynomial raising matrix. Kernel dimension there is dimE0, so at every weight the kernel dimension is at least dimE0. The existing restriction and growth upper bound remains unchanged.

items.title: Wall-crossing acts on standard modules by a two-step extension
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. Let
$\theta_s$ be the wall-crossing functor of
[[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] attached to the simple reflection
$s$ in the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$. For every $w\in W$ the
object $\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ has a finite Verma flag with exactly two
factors, namely $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ and $\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)$, each with
multiplicity one; in the Grothendieck group
$$[\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]=[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)].$$
Moreover $\theta_s$ is exact and preserves Verma-filtered objects with finite
Verma flags: if $X$ has a finite Verma flag with multiplicities
$(X:\Delta(v\cdot\lambda))$, then $\theta_sX$ has one with multiplicities
$(\theta_sX:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))=(X:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))+(X:\Delta(us\cdot\lambda))$,
and the same formula holds in $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$. The resulting flag is
not in general split; splitting is neither asserted nor used.
items.strategy: Use the finite-dimensional tensor weight filtration and the norm comparison: translating a regular standard onto the s-wall retains precisely the one singular standard at the same coset, and translating it out retains the two regular labels w and ws, once each. The dominant-representative convention is established directly by the same published dominant norm-distance and extremal-weight argument (the printed single-wall datum uses antidominant representatives); changing to the dominant orbit representative reverses Bruhat labels. Exactness concatenates these two-factor flags across a finite Verma flag of X, proving the stated multiplicity formula. The two-step object need not split. No assertion that arbitrary subquotients of Verma-filtered objects are Verma-filtered is used.

items.title: Base change, freeness and specialization in the deformed family
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. In the deformed family of
[[def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-its-specializations]] with $T$ a
localization of $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ and $M,N\in\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$:

1. The canonical map
$$U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_ZT\longrightarrow\bigl(\operatorname{End}_T(M_T(\lambda))\bigr)^{\mathfrak g\text{-finite}},\qquad u\otimes t\longmapsto\bigl(m\mapsto u\cdot m\cdot t\bigr),$$
is an isomorphism of $T$-algebras, the superscript denoting the $\mathfrak g$-finite part for the adjoint action $X\cdot f=X\circ f-f\circ X$, and the center $Z=Z(U(\mathfrak g))$ acting on $T$ through the shifted Harish-Chandra isomorphism $\operatorname{HC}_\rho$ ([[thm-harish-chandra-isomorphism-for-the-center]]) followed by evaluation at $\lambda+\rho+\epsilon$ on the universal parameter $\epsilon$.
2. For finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-modules $E,F$, the $T$-module
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(E\otimes M_T(\lambda),F\otimes M_T(\lambda))$
is free of rank $\dim(E\otimes F^{*})_0$, and the natural base-change map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(M,N)\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes\kappa(\epsilon)}(M\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon),N\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon))$$
is an isomorphism for every $\epsilon\in\operatorname{Spec}T$.
3. $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(M,N)$ is locally free of finite rank over $T$.
4. If a $\mathfrak g\otimes R$-linear map of objects of $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ is an isomorphism on the special fiber at $0$, it is an isomorphism.
items.strategy: Use the locally proved Duflo–Joseph theorem in every field fiber and the exact adjoint zero-weight-rank lemma. For each finite-dimensional E, Hom(M_S(lambda),E tensor M_S(lambda)) is the kernel of the finitely many simple-raising maps on the finite free relative lambda-weight space; PBW bases make their matrices polynomial in the parameter. Every closed fiber has dimension dim E_0 by the field theorem. Thus every (s+1)-minor vanishes and the s-minors generate the unit ideal, where s is the constant matrix rank: vanishing follows from polynomial evaluation at all complex points, and a proper minor ideal would lie in a maximal ideal. On each invertible s-minor chart, Gaussian elimination puts the matrix in diag(I_s,0), proving that its kernel is finite projective, locally split and commutes with every base change, including residue fields of nonclosed primes. Tensor adjunction identifies this kernel with the appropriate finite adjoint isotypic endomorphisms. The action source is finite free of the same zero-weight rank by harmonic isotypic freeness; its closed-fiber maps are the Duflo–Joseph isomorphisms, so its finite cokernel vanishes by local Nakayama at every maximal ideal, and the equal-rank projective kernel vanishes as well. Hence action is an isomorphism on every isotypic over S and, by local finiteness, on all g-finite endomorphisms. The same finite matrices and flat localization give every T localization. For tensor objects E tensor M and F tensor M, adjunction reduces Hom to the same finite highest-weight kernel for E* tensor F, proving the stated rank and specialization. Direct summands take images of split idempotents in these Hom modules, preserving finite projectivity/local freeness and all base-change isomorphisms. Over local R the weight spaces are finite free; a g⊗R-linear residue isomorphism is invertible weight by weight by the determinant/Nakayama argument. This algebraic route replaces the imported universal differential-operator theorem and the Jantzen7.25 fallback without dropping any all-T or all-weight assertion.

items.title: The wall-crossing action on the Grothendieck group is multiplication by 1+s
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. In the
regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ of
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] the
assignment
$$c\colon K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z[W],\qquad[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]\longmapsto w,$$
is an isomorphism of abelian groups, and for every simple reflection $s$ the
wall-crossing functor $\theta_s$ of
[[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] satisfies
$$c\,[\theta_sX]=c\,[X]\cdot(1+s)\qquad\text{for all }X\in\mathcal O_\lambda,$$
right multiplication by $1+s$ in the integral group ring $\mathbb Z[W]$.
Consequently, for a reduced word $w=s_1\cdots s_k$ one has
$$c\,[\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}\Delta(\lambda)]=(1+s_1)(1+s_2)\cdots(1+s_k),$$
the sum of all subexpression products with their actual multiplicities; its top
Bruhat term is $w$ once and all other terms have strictly smaller labels. With
the composition $\theta_{s_1}\cdots\theta_{s_k}$ instead, the factors are
multiplied in the reverse order.
items.strategy: The class of any object is the sum of the classes of the factors of a finite Verma flag, and [[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]] gives that the Verma classes form a basis; since the block has $|W|$ Verma classes indexed by $W$, the assignment is an isomorphism of free abelian groups. The formula $[\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]=[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)]$ of [[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-standard-modules-by-the-two-step-extension]], applied factor by factor using exactness of $\theta_s$, gives $c[\theta_s X]=c[X]\cdot(1+s)$ on the Verma basis, hence on the whole group; the right multiplication by $s$ acts by $w\mapsto ws$ on the basis, giving the displayed convention. Composition applies its rightmost functor first, so iteration gives the reverse functor order and the product of (1+s_i), not the single group element w. The full reduced subexpression is the unique one of maximal length; proper subexpressions have smaller Bruhat labels, with multiplicities that can exceed one.

items.title: Wall-crossing compositions produce the projective with the top standard label
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a dominant regular integral representative
$\lambda$ and a reduced word $w=s_1\cdots s_k$, set
$\theta_{\underline w}=\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}$, so that the standards
follow right multiplication in word order. Then
$$\theta_{\underline w}\Delta(\lambda)\cong P(w\cdot\lambda)\oplus\bigoplus_{x<w}P(x\cdot\lambda)^{m_x},\qquad m_x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.$$
Its class is $(1+s_1)\cdots(1+s_k)$ under the standard class map, with actual
subexpression multiplicities. The BGG matrix satisfies
$(P(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=[\Delta(y\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)]$,
vanishes unless $y\le x$ in the Bruhat order, and has diagonal entries one.
Hence the top summand $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ occurs once and is the only summand
whose flag contains $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$; the remaining multiplicities are
determined by this triangular matrix and the product class. Consequently every
indecomposable projective is a summand of a word of wall crossings applied to
$\Delta(\lambda)$.
items.strategy: The dominant Verma is projective in its block, since its Hom functor is its maximal weight space; exact biadjoint wall crossing preserves projectives. Thus the word object decomposes into indecomposable projective covers. Its standard class is the subexpression product from the corrected right-action lemma. The full reduced subexpression contributes w once and all other subexpressions are below w. Strong linkage and BGG reciprocity give the Bruhat-triangular projective matrix with standard support y<=x and diagonal one for the dominant representative. A maximal head outside the class support would contribute its own standard with positive coefficient, impossible, so only x<=w occur. The coefficient of Delta_w forces P_w once. The remaining coefficients are determined successively. Nonnegativity follows from the actual projective decomposition, not an assumed all-one interval character. Explicitly, a strong-linkage reflection with positive integral pairing sends a dominant-orbit label x to s_alpha x with larger Bruhat label, by the positive-root reflection-descent criterion and subword/deletion property. This proves the required reversal of the weight order and the Bruhat standard-support triangle; proper subexpressions reduce by deletion to subwords of w.
