items.title: Lifting of indecomposable projectives to the deformed family
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be dominant regular integral,
$R=S(\mathfrak h)_{(0)}$ the localization at the origin, and use the selected
component $\mathcal D_R^{[\lambda]}(\lambda)$ of the tensor-generated deformed
family of [[def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-its-specializations]]. For
every $x\in W$ there is a projective $P_R(x,\lambda)$ in the deformed
$\lambda$-block whose residue fiber is $P(x\cdot\lambda)$; it is unique up to
isomorphism, and every indecomposable of this selected tensor component is one
of these lifts. Each lift has a finite deformed Verma flag with the same
multiplicities as its closed fiber. More generally, a finite projective in this
block is a direct summand of a finite sum of truncated induced projectives
representing relative weight spaces; for every map of deformation algebras
$R\to R'$ its base change is projective in the corresponding truncated category
and
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_R}(P,N)\otimes_RR'\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{R'}}(P\otimes_RR',N\otimes_RR').$$
For a finite Verma-filtered target $N$ this Hom module is finite free over
local $R$. A $\mathfrak g\otimes R$-linear map between such finite
projective/Verma-filtered objects whose residue fiber is an isomorphism is
itself an isomorphism, weight by weight. For a dot-dominant integral target
$\nu$, including singular $\nu$, the same local projective construction gives
all lifts in its deformed block, with labels the distinct cosets $W/W_\nu$;
these lifts belong to the target component $\mathcal D_R^{[\nu]}(\lambda)$ of a
regular-source tensor family. It is neither necessary nor asserted that the
singular Verma itself generates every target projective, and the other central
components of the full tensor family are not claimed to have only these
indecomposables.
items.strategy:
Use the independent local construction recorded in the owner proof note, rather than the universal g-finite endomorphism theorem. For $\xi\le\lambda$, truncate the positive PBW weights of $U(\mathfrak b)$ above $\lambda-\xi$, tensor its finite right-$U(\mathfrak h)$-free quotient with the deformed rank-one weight $\xi$, and induce to $\mathfrak g$. The resulting $Q_R(\xi)$ has a finite Verma flag and represents the weight functor $N\mapsto N^\xi$ on weights $\le\lambda$: evaluate at the cyclic tensor generator; all excluded positive monomials kill a vector of weight $\xi$. Thus it is projective and its Hom functor commutes with arbitrary algebra base change. The same holds for finite sums and direct summands, by taking images of split weight-space idempotents. To isolate a central component, choose $z$ separating the finitely many special characters in the flag. Group its annihilating factors $X-\operatorname{HC}_ho(z)(
u+ho+	au)$ by special character. Pairwise resultants are units of $R$; the Sylvester adjugate supplies Bezout identities, and Chinese remaindering yields actual polynomial central projectors over $R$. No completion is assumed. A direct summand of a local deformed Verma flag is Verma-filtered: for a maximal label $
u$, the canonical submodule $U(\mathfrak g)X^
u=\Delta_R(
u)\otimes_R X^
u$ has Verma-filtered quotient. Prove this by induction on the original flag, splitting a last quotient labelled $
u$ by a lifted highest vector. Every projector preserves this canonical submodule; its top-weight image is finite free over local $R$, and induction on the quotient proves the assertion. Now induct orbit weights downward. The selected $Q_R(\xi)$ has special fiber containing $P(\xi)$ once and only $P(\eta)$ with $\eta>\xi$ otherwise, since $\operatorname{Hom}(Q_0(\xi),L(\eta))=L(\eta)^\xi$. Lift the inclusion and retraction of the already constructed higher-label sum using the proved projective Hom base-change law. Their composite is $1$ modulo the maximal ideal in a finite $R$-End algebra. Left and right multiplication by this composite have finite cokernels killed by Nakayama, so it has a two-sided inverse. Correct the retraction by that inverse and take the complementary projective summand; it specializes to $P(\xi)$. This constructs every lift; lifting inverse maps proves uniqueness by the same finite-End argument, and free flag quotients preserve multiplicities. Finite-dimensional tensoring and central projection are exact biadjoint functors over $R$ by the tensor-Hom pairing, so they preserve projectives. The dominant deformed Verma represents its top weight in its block. For the regular block, ordinary wall-word object generation is proved first from two-step flags and BGG. Its deformed word is projective and specializes to the same projective word, so local lift uniqueness identifies its summands with the constructed lifts. This proves membership in the fixed regular-source tensor family without invoking the later functor classifier. For a dot-dominant singular target nu, construct its lifts by the same truncated-projective induction. Choose sigma=nu+N rho regular dominant so large that sigma-mu is dominant for every mu in its finite orbit. Tensor M_R(sigma) with the finite-dimensional simple having lowest extremal weight mu-sigma. In its selected target component, all retained standard labels are at least mu and mu occurs once; BGG and projective decomposition therefore give P(mu) once. Projective Hom base change lifts that splitting to the constructed P_R(mu). Thus all singular lifts lie in the regular-source sigma tensor family. The dominant norm-distance argument translates the regular standard M_R(lambda) to M_R(sigma) with one retained factor and conversely, so the two tensor families agree: nested natural block projectors remain summands of the product finite-dimensional tensor. The singular target component has all these coset-labelled projectives, and its indecomposable objects are exactly them by lifting its finite residual projective decomposition. This is the true regular-source singular-target assertion. This proves the local projective interface; it does not prove the separate all-localizations universal-Verma Kostant assertion.

items.title: Indecomposable projective functors are indexed by the Weyl group
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral block with dominant
representative $\lambda$:

1. Projective functors form a Krull-Schmidt category.
2. Their indecomposables are indexed by $W$, with $\Theta_w$ characterized by
$\Theta_w\Delta(\lambda)\cong P(w\cdot\lambda)$. For a reduced word
$w=s_1\cdots s_k$, the functor $\Theta_w$ is a multiplicity-one summand of
$\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}$, and every other indecomposable summand has a
label $x<w$. In particular every indecomposable projective functor is generated
as a summand by wall crossings.
3. Two projective functors are naturally equivalent exactly when their induced
operators on the Grothendieck group agree.

The characterization concerns evaluation on the dominant projective Verma; no
faithfulness of that evaluation on all natural maps of arbitrary
endofunctors is asserted.
items.strategy: Evaluation of natural maps on the dominant Verma is surjective, not necessarily injective on ordinary O. For ambient tensor functors, a map E tensor M(lambda)->F tensor M(lambda) is a finite adjoint matrix coefficient in End M(lambda); Duflo–Joseph identifies it with a g-equivariant matrix in U_chi. The harmonic isotypic free decomposition lifts that matrix to U, giving a U-bimodule map E tensor U->F tensor U and hence a natural tensor-functor map on all modules. Compose the exact block projections and summand inclusions/retractions to obtain surjectivity for all projective functors. The evaluation kernel is nilpotent: every standard Delta_y embeds in the dominant Delta_e, so exactness and naturality make a map vanishing on Delta_e vanish on every standard. On a fixed projective generator with a Verma flag of length k it strictly lowers the induced flag; k-fold compositions vanish. Evaluation at that generator is faithful for natural maps on exact functors because every object has a finite projective presentation. It also proves finite-dimensionality of natural End spaces. Hence the kernel on every finite additive functor sum is a nilpotent ideal. Idempotents lift across a nilpotent ideal by correcting a lift modulo successive powers (or the explicit polynomial idempotent-lifting formula); isomorphisms lift because 1 plus a nilpotent-kernel element is invertible by a finite geometric series. Therefore decompositions and isomorphism classes of projective functors are exactly those of their dominant-Verma evaluations. Finite-dimensional End algebras and split idempotents give Krull–Schmidt; indecomposable local End rings correspond through the nilpotent kernel. The corrected wall-word projective-generation lemma realizes every P_w and gives the new multiplicity-one functor Theta_w. If two K0 operators agree, their dominant-Verma evaluations are projectives with the same class, hence the same indecomposable multiplicities by BGG unitriangularity; lift their isomorphism to the functors. The converse is formal. Central nilpotent natural endomorphisms of the identity vanish on Delta_e, so no false full-faithfulness assertion for this evaluation is made.

items.title: The central action on the deformed antidominant projective
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be dominant regular integral,
$S=S(\mathfrak h)$, $R=S_{(0)}$, and $P_R=P_R(w_0,\lambda)$ the deformed
antidominant projective. Write $\operatorname{HC}_\rho\colon Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to S^W$
for the published shifted Harish-Chandra isomorphism,
$\sigma_\lambda(f)(\epsilon)=f(\lambda+\rho+\epsilon)$, and define
$$a_\lambda\colon Z\otimes_{\mathbb C}R\longrightarrow R\otimes_{R^W}R,\qquad z\otimes r\longmapsto\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z))\otimes r.$$
Then $a_\lambda$ and the action map $Z\otimes R\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes R}(P_R)$
are surjective and have the same kernel, inducing a canonical $R$-algebra
isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes R}(P_R)\cong R\otimes_{R^W}R.$$
On a generic Verma constituent of highest weight $x\cdot\lambda+\epsilon$, $z$
acts by the scalar
$\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z)(x(\lambda+\rho)+\epsilon)=\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z))(x^{-1}\epsilon)$;
these scalars vary with $x$, and the center need not act by a single scalar on
$P_R$. After tensoring the right $R$ factor with the residue field at $0$, the
endomorphism algebra becomes $C=S/(S^W_+S)$. More generally, for dot-dominant
integral $\nu$ the corresponding algebra is $R^{W_\nu}\otimes_{R^W}R$, where
$W_\nu$ is the dot stabilizer. Translation out of that facet identifies the
singular antidominant projective with the regular one; under these shifted
Harish-Chandra identifications, its induced endomorphism map is the inclusion
$R^{W_\nu}\otimes_{R^W}R\hookrightarrow R\otimes_{R^W}R$.
items.strategy: The complete algebraic local-order proof is recorded in the owner central-order note. First the most-singular translation Q has each distinct block Verma once. It contains P_antidominant as a split summand; every standard contains its simple antidominant Verma, so BGG reciprocity forces every flag multiplicity of P to be one and Q=P. The local projective theorem gives the same free flag for P_R and arbitrary Hom base change. Generically its constituents have distinct central characters and End(P_K) is the tuple algebra. At a height-one nonroot prime they remain distinct. At a root prime alpha, the residual central characters split into pairs {x,s_alpha x}, or singletons in the singular case. The symbolic generic-hyperplane Shapovalov/Casimir proof gives the upper Verma length2 and the lower Verma simple. The localized projective pair has those two flag factors once; its residue cannot split, since the lower simple Verma is nonprojective (dualizing the upper length2 Verma supplies a nonsplit extension ending in it). Any endomorphism preserves the maximal-weight Verma and has two scalar eigenvalues congruent mod alpha; otherwise its residual polynomial projector would split the extension. Their Casimir eigenvalues differ by n(alpha,alpha)tau(alpha^vee), a unit times the DVR parameter. Thus identity and Casimir generate precisely the full congruence order. Finite central polynomial projectors isolate different pairs. Independently R tensor_{R^W}R has the same local orders: CRT separates distinct graph branches, and a linear polynomial with nonzero root-normal coefficient generates the within-pair uniformizer difference. It is finite free by invariant freeness; taking first-factor stabilizer invariants gives the singular order. Both this order and End(P_R) are intersections of their height-one localizations in their generic tuple spaces, because they are finite free over the polynomial local ring. They therefore agree globally. To prove shifted central-image surjectivity, for H=Stab(nu+rho) prescribe a desired H-invariant coinvariant jet at nu+rho and zero jets at the other orbit points. Polynomial CRT and the explicit p=(1/|H|)sum_{w in W}q(w^-1 X) produce a W-invariant polynomial with that jet; exactly |H| equal jets survive. Thus shifted HC is onto the closed C^H fiber, and finite-module Nakayama gives surjectivity onto the entire deformed order. Kernels agree by the actual tuple action. Translation out of the facet sends each singular generic branch to its regular coset branches and therefore induces the invariant-order inclusion; its projective identification follows from the norm-comparison standard counts, once-each flag and local lift uniqueness. No generic-only dimension inference, unproved Luna slice theorem or imported universal g-finite theorem is used.

items.title: The endomorphisms of the antidominant projective form the coinvariant algebra
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be finite-dimensional complex
semisimple, $\lambda$ the dominant regular integral representative of a block
and $\mathcal O_\lambda$ its block with antidominant weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$.
Let $C$ be the coinvariant algebra of
[[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]] for the Cartan
reflection representation, with its grading fixed there. Then:

(1) the natural maps $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to C$ (Harish-Chandra isomorphism,
shifted by $\lambda+\rho$ in the published $\operatorname{HC}_\rho$ convention,
followed by the quotient map $\rho$) and $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$
(multiplication) are surjective with the same kernel;

(2) consequently the multiplication map induces a canonical algebra isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)\ \cong\ C,$$
identifying $C$ with the endomorphism ring of the antidominant projective,
canonically and independently of the choice of projective cover inside its
isomorphism class;

(3) the grading on the right-hand side is the internal grading of the
coinvariant algebra; no graded lift of category $\mathcal O$ is asserted or
used.

This is Soergel's Endomorphismensatz [Soe90, Theorem 7], in the regular integral
case; the companion general form for singular blocks replaces $C$ by the
invariants $C^{W_\lambda}$.
items.strategy: Apply the deformed central-action lemma with $R=S_{(0)}$ and specialize its right $R$ factor at $0$. Hom base change identifies the specialization with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$, while $(R\otimes_{R^W}R)\otimes_R\mathbb C=R/(R^W_+R)\cong C$; localization does not change this finite-dimensional quotient. The action of $Z$ specializes to the shifted Harish-Chandra quotient map. Thus the two maps are surjective with the same kernel. For singular dominant integral $\lambda$, the same specialization of $R^{W_\lambda}\otimes_{R^W}R$ gives $C^{W_\lambda}$. The proof depends on the full integral deformed central-action theorem; neither a generic dimension count nor citation of the Endomorphismensatz itself supplies it.

items.title: Soergel's Struktursatz: the functor V is fully faithful on projectives
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be a regular integral block
with antidominant projective $P=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ and Soergel functor
$V=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,-)$, and let $C$ be the coinvariant
algebra, identified with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ by
[[thm-endomorphisms-of-the-antidominant-projective-are-the-coinvariant-algebra]],
so that $V$ takes values in $C$-modules. Then for every $M\in\mathcal O_\lambda$
and every projective $Q\in\mathcal O_\lambda$ the canonical map
$$V\colon \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_\lambda}(M,Q)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{C\text{-mod}}(VM,VQ)$$
is an isomorphism. In particular $V$ is fully faithful on the full subcategory
of projective objects of the block, and it is faithful on all of
$\mathcal O_\lambda$ after passing to the quotient by the Serre subcategory of
objects killed by $V$.
items.strategy: Use the complete ordinary argument in the owner dictionary note. P is the indecomposable projective-injective with antidominant essential socle; every projective-injective is a sum of P, since a simple embedded in a Verma must be the antidominant simple and this property passes through flags. The proved coinvariant top pairing makes C a Frobenius algebra, hence injective as its own module. For simple M the canonical Hom(M,P)->Hom_C(VM,C) is zero off the antidominant label and a nonzero one-dimensional map on it; both functors are exact, so finite composition-series induction gives the isomorphism for every M. Maximal-weight peeling puts Delta_dominant in P with Verma-filtered quotient. It is exactly the C_+-annihilated part: if that part were larger, its quotient would contain the antidominant simple, giving dimension>=2 under exact V, but its image in VP=C lies in the one-dimensional socle. Taking annihilated Hom subspaces gives Hom(M,Delta_dominant)=Hom_C(VM,VDelta_dominant). For a word F of wall functors, the exact adjoint word G sends P to sums of P, hence both preserve ker V. The exact quotient by ker V is C-mod: the left adjoint P tensor_C - has V of it equal to the identity, and the counit's kernel/cokernel are killed by V. The adjunction descends, so Hom(M,FDelta)=Hom(GM,Delta)=Hom_C(VGM,VDelta)=Hom_C(VM,VFDelta). Ordinary wall-word object generation supplies every projective as a summand, proving the assertion and quotient-faithfulness clause. This uses object generation, not an unnecessary functor-classification prerequisite or an unproved quotient-adjunction lemma.

items.title: Wall-crossing under the Soergel functor is tensoring with the coinvariant bimodule
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a regular integral block and simple reflection
$s$, with $C=\operatorname{End}(P(w_0\cdot\lambda))$, there is a natural
isomorphism of functors to left $C$-modules
$$V\theta_s\cong C\otimes_{C^s}V.$$
Equivalently the functor is tensoring by the $(C,C)$-bimodule
$C\otimes_{C^s}C$, with left action on the first factor and right action on the
second. In type A over $\mathbb C$, its polynomial lift is tensoring on the
left by $B_s=S\otimes_{S^s}S(1)$; read up to the auxiliary suspension
normalisation fixed by the rank-one case, the right origin reduction of $B_s$
is the two-dimensional module of centered degrees $-1,1$, for $M=S$ the
coinvariant reduction satisfies
$B_s\otimes_SC\cong(C\otimes_{C^s}C)(1)$ in the same normalisation, and
$B_s\otimes_S\mathbb C$ itself is not the bimodule $C\otimes_{C^s}C$: the
former has vector-space dimension two, whereas the latter has dimension
$2|W|$. Forgetting the grading gives the displayed category-$\mathcal O$
formula, and no grading on arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects is asserted.
items.strategy: The complete ordinary/deformed translation argument is in the owner dictionary note. Let H={1,s}. Dominant norm-distance and finite-dimensional extremal-weight bounds give one retained standard onto the facet and two out. Out translation sends the singular antidominant projective to the regular one, since its flag has every regular standard once and adjunction gives its antidominant cover quotient; over R local lift uniqueness proves the same identification. Its End map is the inclusion of invariant orders, checked on generic constituents. Onto translation of the regular antidominant projective is two copies of the singular one: ordinarily it is projective-injective, hence a sum of that projective, and its flag counts give two; over R local projective uniqueness lifts this, without claiming R-injectivity. Therefore V_singular T_on=Res V_regular by adjunction, and both translations preserve the V-killed subcategories. The explicit quotient equivalence from P tensor_A - and its counit descends the biadjunction; extension of scalars is adjoint to restriction, so V_regular T_out=Ind V_singular. Compose to get C tensor_{C^s}V, or the corresponding deformed R tensor_{R^s} action. The image of S^s in C is C^s by averaging representatives. Tensor reduction and the rank-two free S/S^s basis identify the polynomial B_s action, with the chosen shift; its two-dimensional right origin reduction is distinct from the 2|W|-dimensional coinvariant bimodule.

items.title: Indecomposable projectives correspond to indecomposable Soergel modules
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and work in a regular integral type-A block over
$\mathbb C$. With the page's right wall-crossing convention and left
$C$-module values of $V$, there is an equivalence
$$V\colon\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal O_\lambda)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{\text{ungraded Soergel modules }B\otimes_S\mathbb C\},\qquad P(w\cdot\lambda)\longmapsto\bar B_{w^{-1}}.$$
The target is the additive category of direct summands of the right reductions
of polynomial Bott-Samelson bimodules, or equivalently of iterated
$C\otimes_{C^s}(-)$ applied to the trivial module $\mathbb C$, not to the
regular module $C$. For $w=s_1\cdots s_k$, the projective is the unique new
top-label summand of $\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}\Delta(\lambda)$; applying
$V$ gives the new summand of $\overline{B_{s_k}\cdots B_{s_1}}$, thus the
inverse label. These normalized indecomposable polynomial lifts supply
self-dual auxiliary gradings; in rank one the centered degrees are $-1,1$,
with degrees $0,2$ after an uncentered shift. Forgetting grading recovers the
projective dictionary. More generally the ungraded equivalence with
Weyl-group Soergel modules holds for every complex semisimple regular integral
block; the type-A diagrammatic label comparison applies only in type A.
items.strategy: The full local reduction proof is in the owner dictionary note. First prove deformed V full faithfulness on projectives by height-one intersection. In a root DVR the two projectives are upper Verma P_a and pair projective P_b. Their mixed Hom modules have rank one; choose inclusion i and a lift j of the primitive residual map to the upper Verma. The nonzero nilpotent ij and identity form an End(P_b) basis by Nakayama. In the proved congruence order ij=(h,0), so h is a unit times alpha; rescale to ji=alpha. V sends the four Hom modules to precisely the Hom modules between the congruence order and its upper rank-one branch, with i mapping to (alpha,0) and j to projection. At nonroot primes the calculation is one-label Morita. Ordinary projective Hom is finite free over R, and A-module Hom of the finite free V-values is the intersection of its localizations by its finite generator equations; equality at all height-one primes proves full faithfulness over R. Polynomial Bott-Samelson bimodules localized on the right at0 carry the deformed central-order action and are V_R of the translated projective words. Their left denominators nonzero at0 invert on the finite right-free module by Nakayama; invariant left/right actions agree. Finite presentation of polynomial bimodule Hom and flat localization give Hom_A equal to localized polynomial Hom. Deformed full faithfulness, projective Hom base change to0, and ordinary Struktursatz consequently prove the natural reduction-of-Hom isomorphism for Bott-Samelson objects and their summands. This supplies the local proof of Garnier's reduction theorem. For complex extension, the rational polynomial degree-zero End algebra is local with residue Q; its nilpotent radical extends to a nilpotent ideal with quotient C, so remains local. The reduced degree-zero End is a quotient and local. Its finite full Z-graded End is local too: its Jacobson radical is graded by scaling/Vandermonde projections; the semisimple quotient is a product of matrices. The grading derivation on each matrix algebra is inner (c=sum D(E_i1)E_1i gives [c,E_ab]=D(E_ab)); diagonalizability of the derivation makes its degree-zero centralizer semisimple. It is also a quotient of a local algebra, hence C, forcing the whole semisimple quotient to be C. Thus reductions are indecomposable after forgetting grading. Induct on Bruhat length. For the reversed reduced word of w, every proper subexpression has label y<w; its polynomial indecomposable summands B_y, and the projective summands P_{y^-1}, have already been matched by induction. The polynomial B_w occurs once and its reduction is indecomposable; the projective P_{w^-1} occurs once by the object-generation lemma. All remaining projective summands have smaller labels. Finite Krull-Schmidt uniqueness matches the two remaining new summands, and full faithfulness ensures distinct projective labels never become isomorphic. Composition on standards follows right multiplication, while polynomial tensors act on the left, giving the inverse label w^-1. The actual invariant-intersection-form supplier supplies a nondegenerate centered reduced invariant form on each real B_w, not merely a polynomial self-duality assertion. This form descends to the rational reduction: its invariance equations are finite rational linear equations; their rational solution space extends to the real one, and the determinant polynomial is not identically zero, so over the infinite field Q a nondegenerate rational solution exists. Extending that solution to C preserves its determinant and identifies the centered reduction with its graded dual. These normalized lifts therefore supply the claimed auxiliary self-dual grading. For the permutation realization S=Q[x_1,...,x_n], split off the W-fixed average coordinate from the sl_n Cartan; it acts identically on both sides, and polynomial extension/right reduction kills it, so it changes neither the modules nor the Hom comparison. Products of type-A factors follow by tensoring the same finite projective-generator construction. No full Ext grading on O is asserted. Any two finite graded lifts with the same indecomposable underlying C-module differ by a shift: decompose an ungraded isomorphism f and its inverse g into finitely many homogeneous components. The degree-zero identity is sum_d g_{-d}f_d. Since the degree-zero End algebra is local, some g_{-d}f_d is a unit. That f_d is a split graded injection, and ungraded indecomposability of the target forces it to be a graded isomorphism after shift. For finite support, a nonzero shift of a centered self-dual module cannot remain centered self-dual, by the symmetry of its extreme degrees; thus the centered normalization is unique.

items.title: Verma-flag multiplicities are standard-filtration ranks under V
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a projective $P$ in a regular integral type-A
block, choose its polynomial Soergel lift $\mathsf B(P)$ determined by the
preceding projective dictionary: if $P=\bigoplus_wP(w\cdot\lambda)^{m_w}$, take
$\mathsf B(P)=\bigoplus_wB_{w^{-1}}^{m_w}$, so that its right reduction is
$V(P)$ after forgetting auxiliary grading. Write $r_{x,d}(\mathsf B(P))$ for
the graded multiplicity of the polynomial standard graph module supported at
$x$ in its standard support filtration, with the standard-generator
normalization of the polynomial Soergel category. Then
$$(P:\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=\sum_d r_{y^{-1},d}(\mathsf B(P)).$$
Equivalently the polynomial Soergel character of this lift, evaluated at $v=1$
and with inverse labels, recovers the ordinary Verma-flag character of $P$.
These are ranks before reduction; no separated Bruhat-support filtration
intrinsic to the finite-dimensional module $V(P)$ is asserted, since the graph
supports coalesce at the origin. The same ungraded multiplicity comparison
holds with the corresponding Weyl-group polynomial/deformed lifts in other
complex semisimple types.
items.strategy: The exact individual-rank proof is in the owner dictionary note. Deform the projective using the constructive local projective theorem and its flag/Hom base change. V_R is exact and sends each standard Delta_R(y dot lambda) to a finite free R-module of rank one, since the closed Hom dimension is [Delta_y:L_antidominant]=1, already proved by the once-each antidominant flag and BGG. Central action on that standard is f->f(y^-1 tau). In the published polynomial graph convention R_x has left coordinate x times the right parameter, so this is the graph label x=y^-1. Deformed wall crossing and the proved reduced-Hom/indecomposable dictionary identify the right-localized chosen polynomial lift B(P) with V_R P_R. After passage to the fraction field, its x-graph ranks are therefore exactly the Verma multiplicities at y=x^-1. Flat localization preserves polynomial support ranks; summing their graded multiplicities gives those ordinary ranks. The deformed flag specializes exactly, yielding the displayed comparison for every individual y at v=1. Right origin reduction supplies V(P) but collapses all graph supports, so no intrinsic labelled reduced filtration is used. The fixed permutation-realization coordinate is split off as in the preceding dictionary.

items.title: The coinvariant algebra of S_2 and S_3 as graded regular representations
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. We
work over $\mathbb k=\mathbb C$ and compute the coinvariant algebra of
[[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]] in the two smallest
cases and read off its graded decomposition, checking the general theorem
[[thm-the-weyl-coinvariant-algebra-is-the-graded-regular-representation]]; the
example is a verification in small rank and is not used as evidence for the
general statement.

**The case $W=S_2$.** Here $r=1$, the auxiliary polynomial ring is
$\mathbb k[x]$ with the transposition acting by $x\mapsto-x$, and the basic invariant is $x^2$, so
$$C=\mathbb k[x]/(x^2)$$ with $\deg x=2$ in the page normalization and
$\deg x=1$ for the classical Hilbert series. The Hilbert series is therefore
$1+t^2$ in page degrees (equivalently $1+t$ in classical degrees), agreeing
with $\prod_i(1+t^2+\cdots+t^{2(d_i-1)})$ for the single basic degree $d_1=2$
of [[lem-weyl-coinvariant-hilbert-series-has-order-w-dimension]]. The
degree-zero piece $C_0=\mathbb k$ is the trivial representation, and the
one-dimensional top piece $C_2=\mathbb k x$ is the sign representation, so $C$
is the regular representation of $S_2$ with graded multiplicities one for the
trivial and one for the sign module.

**The case $W=S_3$.** Use the auxiliary permutation model of
[[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]:
$$C=\mathbb k[x_1,x_2,x_3]/(e_1,e_2,e_3),\qquad e_1=x_1+x_2+x_3,\ e_2=x_1x_2+x_1x_3+x_2x_3,\ e_3=x_1x_2x_3,$$
with $S_3$ permuting the variables. In classical degrees the basic degrees are
$1,2,3$, so the Hilbert series is
$$\frac{(1-t)(1-t^2)(1-t^3)}{(1-t)^3}=(1+t)(1+t+t^2)=1+2t+2t^2+t^3,$$
and in the page normalization, where each variable has degree $2$, it becomes
$(1+t^2)(1+t^2+t^4)=1+2t^2+2t^4+t^6$. The graded pieces have dimensions
$1,2,2,1$ in degrees $0,2,4,6$.

**Graded pieces as $S_3$-modules.** Identify $C$ with the coinvariant algebra of
the two-dimensional reflection representation $\mathfrak h\subset\mathbb k^3$.
The degree-zero piece $C_0$ is the trivial module. The degree-two piece $C_2$
is spanned by the images of $x_1,x_2,x_3$ modulo $e_1$; these span a
two-dimensional space on which $S_3$ acts as the standard reflection
representation. Put $a=x_1$, $b=x_2$, $x_3=-a-b$. The relations are
$a^2+ab+b^2=0$ and $a^2b+ab^2=0$, so $b^3=0$ and
$C_6$ is spanned by the nonzero class $ab^2$ (its nonvanishing also follows
from the Hilbert series). The Vandermonde reduces to $-6ab^2$, so it spans
$C_6$ and carries the sign character. The perfect multiplication pairing
$C_2\times C_4\to C_6$ from
[[lem-the-coinvariant-algebra-is-a-gorenstein-algebra-with-one-dimensional-socle]]
identifies $C_4$ with $C_2^*\otimes\mathrm{sign}$. The standard reflection
representation is self-dual: the invariant coordinate dot product restricts
nondegenerately to the sum-zero plane. Hence $C_4$ is standard tensor sign. Thus
$$C_0=\text{trivial},\quad C_2=\text{standard},\quad C_4=\text{standard}\otimes\text{sign},\quad C_6=\text{sign},$$
the graded lift of the regular representation, with graded multiplicities
$1$ for the trivial module, $t^6$ for the sign module and $t^2+t^4$ for the
two-dimensional standard module.

**Character check.** By
[[thm-the-weyl-coinvariant-algebra-is-the-graded-regular-representation]] the
graded character is
$$\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)(w)=\prod_{i=1}^r(1-t^{2d_i})\det(1-t^2w\mid\mathfrak h^*)^{-1}.$$
For a transposition in $S_3$ the eigenvalues on $\mathfrak h^*$ are $1,-1$, so
$\det(1-t^2w)=(1-t^2)(1+t^2)=1-t^4$ and the quotient is
$(1-t^4)(1-t^6)/(1-t^4)=1-t^6$, matching the direct sum
$1+0\cdot t^2+0\cdot t^4+(-1)t^6$. For a three-cycle the eigenvalues are the
primitive cube roots $\omega,\omega^2$, so $\det(1-t^2w)=1+t^2+t^4$ and the
quotient is $(1-t^4)(1-t^6)/(1+t^2+t^4)=(1-t^2)(1-t^4)=1-t^2-t^4+t^6$, matching
$1+(-1)t^2+(-1)t^4+t^6$. At $w=1$ the quotient is
$1+2t^2+2t^4+t^6$ and its value at $t=1$ is $6=|S_3|$. In both cases the
graded character at $t=1$ is the character of the regular representation, and
the sum of graded multiplicities times dimensions is
$1+2+2+1=6=|W|$, respectively $1+1=2=|S_2|$, as the general theorem asserts.
items.strategy: Direct computation of the quotient by the basic invariants in the given coordinates; the Hilbert series is [[lem-weyl-coinvariant-hilbert-series-has-order-w-dimension]] with the basic degrees $1,2$ (respectively $1,2,3$); the identification of the graded pieces with the named $S_n$-modules is by comparing characters at the transpositions and the three-cycle, and the conclusion is the general theorem. The example is a verification of the general statement in the smallest cases and is not used as evidence for it.

items.title: The wall-crossing functor on Verma modules in rank one
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Work in $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ with the conventions of
[[def-bgg-category-o]]: $\lambda=0$, $\rho=1$, so the regular standards are
$\Delta_1=M(0)$ and $\Delta_s=M(-2)$ for the two elements of
$W=\{1,s\}$, and the singular wall weight is $\mu=-1$, whose shifted value is
$\mu+\rho=0$. The dominant regular integral block is that of $\lambda=0$
([[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]]), and
the wall-crossing functor is that of
[[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] built from the two-dimensional
translating module $E=L(1)$ with highest weight $\mu-\lambda=-1$ up to Weyl
conjugacy.

**Onto the wall.** Tensoring the two regular standards with the two-dimensional
module and projecting to the central character of the wall preserves the
unique wall standard: $T_{\mathrm{on}}\Delta_1\cong M(-1)$ and
$T_{\mathrm{on}}\Delta_s\cong M(-1)$, since $\Delta_1$ and $\Delta_s$ differ by
the single simple-root lowering and the tensor filtration retains exactly the
labels of weight $-1$ in the shifted parametrization, as in
[[thm-translation-to-and-from-a-wall-on-standard-modules]].

**Back out of the wall.** The wall block at $\mu=-1$ has a single simple
object $M(-1)=L(-1)$ and is semisimple; hence $M(-1)$ is projective and
injective there, and the exact biadjoint return translation
$T_{\mathrm{out}}$ sends it to a projective object of the regular block whose
Verma flag has the two factors $M(0)$ and $M(-2)$, once each, by
[[thm-translation-to-and-from-a-wall-on-standard-modules]]. By biadjunction, its Hom to $L(-2)$ is one-dimensional, since
$T_{\mathrm{on}}L(-2)=M(-1)$; its Hom to $L(0)$ is zero, since
$L(1)\otimes L(0)=L(1)$ has a different central character from $M(-1)$.
Thus its only simple quotient is $L(-2)$, once, and the projective-cover
decomposition identifies it with $P(-2)$.

**Conclusion.** Both $\theta_s\Delta_1$ and $\theta_s\Delta_s$ are therefore
isomorphic to the same nonsplit two-step extension
$$0\longrightarrow M(0)\longrightarrow P(-2)\longrightarrow M(-2)\longrightarrow 0,$$
with class $[\Delta_1]+[\Delta_s]$ in the Grothendieck group, in agreement with
[[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-standard-modules-by-the-two-step-extension]].
Maximal-weight peeling puts $M(0)$ first in the flag; the extension is
nonsplit because $P(-2)$ is indecomposable as a projective cover. The wall
sits at highest weight $-1$, equivalently at shifted parameter $\mu+\rho=0$;
the regular highest weight $0$ is the dominant maximum of the block;
the antidominant minimum is $-2$.
items.strategy: Apply the extremal-weight tensor filtration to the natural two-dimensional module and project to the indicated central character. There is one retained wall standard and two retained return standards. The return is projective because M(-1) is the projective simple in its one-simple block and return translation is exact biadjoint. Its once-each flag and antidominant simple quotient identify it with P(-2). Maximal-weight peeling puts M(0) first; nonsplitting follows from indecomposability of that cover. The zero wall is the shifted parameter mu+rho, not the regular highest weight0.

items.title: The class map and the wall-crossing action in rank two
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. Work in
type $A_2$: the Weyl group is $W=S_3=\langle s,t\rangle$ with $s^2=t^2=1$ and
$m_{st}=3$, so that the six elements $1,s,t,st,ts,sts$ are distinct, with
$sts=tst=w_0$. Fix a dominant regular integral weight $\lambda$ and its regular
integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ in the sense of
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]], with
standards $\Delta(v\cdot\lambda)$ indexed by $v\in W$. By
[[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]] the classes
$[\Delta(v\cdot\lambda)]$ form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$,
so the assignment
$$c\colon K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z[W],\qquad c[\Delta(v\cdot\lambda)]=v$$
is an isomorphism of abelian groups, and
[[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-the-grothendieck-group-by-right-multiplication-by-one-plus-s]]
identifies the class action of the wall-crossing functor $\theta_s$ of
[[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] with right multiplication by
$1+s$, and likewise for $t$.

**The two-step products.** Applying the class formula first to
$\Delta(\lambda)$ and then to the one-step object gives
$$c\,[\theta_t\theta_s\Delta(\lambda)]=(1+s)(1+t)=1+s+t+st,$$
because $\theta_s$ acts first and contributes the factor $1+s$ on the right.
The other order gives
$$c\,[\theta_s\theta_t\Delta(\lambda)]=(1+t)(1+s)=1+t+s+ts.$$
Thus
$$[\theta_t\theta_s\Delta(\lambda)]=[\Delta(\lambda)]+[\Delta(s\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(t\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(st\cdot\lambda)]$$
while
$$[\theta_s\theta_t\Delta(\lambda)]=[\Delta(\lambda)]+[\Delta(t\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(s\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ts\cdot\lambda)].$$

**Non-commutativity.** The two products differ: the coefficients of the
length-two elements $st$ and $ts$, which are distinct elements of $S_3$, are
interchanged. Since the Verma classes are linearly independent, the two class
operators on $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$ differ, and in fact they already differ
on the single class $[\Delta(\lambda)]$. This is the same non-commutativity as
in the Hecke algebra of the $S_3$ system, whose standard generators satisfy
$T_sT_t=T_{st}\ne T_{ts}=T_tT_s$; the wall-crossing functors accordingly
behave Hecke-like rather than like a commuting tuple of group elements, and the
two-step products are already sensitive to the order in which the walls are
crossed.

**Projective multiplicities.** The object $\theta_s\theta_t\Delta(\lambda)$ is
projective, and its class contains the single Bruhat-maximal label $ts$ with
coefficient one. By
[[lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-the-projective-with-the-top-standard-label]]
for the reduced word $ts$ (the composite $\theta_s\theta_t$ applies $\theta_t$
first), the indecomposable projective $P(ts\cdot\lambda)$ occurs as a summand
of $\theta_s\theta_t\Delta(\lambda)$ with multiplicity one, and every other
indecomposable summand has a strictly smaller label, i.e. lies among
$P(1),P(s\cdot\lambda),P(t\cdot\lambda)$. The multiplicity of $P(ts\cdot\lambda)$
is read off from the unitriangularity of the standard-support matrix of the
block; the remaining multiplicities are determined recursively but the example
records only the top one.
items.strategy: Read off the class formula from [[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-the-grothendieck-group-by-right-multiplication-by-one-plus-s]] applied first to $\Delta_1$ and then to the two-factor objects; the two computations differ in the label of the length-two factor ($ts$ versus $st$), which are distinct elements of $S_3$ and hence distinct Verma classes by the standard basis theorem [[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]]. The projective multiplicities follow from [[lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-the-projective-with-the-top-standard-label]] for the word ts (since theta_s theta_t applies t first), with the corrected standard-support triangle y<=x of the Verma-flag matrix.

items.title: Wall-crossing functors do not commute
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. In type
$A_2$ with distinct simple reflections $s,t$ (so $m_{st}=3$), the wall-crossing
functors $\theta_s\theta_t$ and $\theta_t\theta_s$ on the regular integral block
commute, so that the assignment $s\mapsto\theta_s$ defines a representation of
$W=S_3$ on the block. This is false: the two functors are not naturally
equivalent, and $\theta_s^2$ is not the identity.
items.strategy: Compute both classes with [[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-the-grothendieck-group-by-right-multiplication-by-one-plus-s]], using that the Verma classes are a basis ([[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]] and the standard-basis theorem for the Grothendieck group); the labels $st$ and $ts$ are distinct elements of $S_3$, and the two induced operators on the standard generators differ, so the induced operators on $K_0$ differ. By the determination theorem [[thm-indecomposable-projective-functors-are-indexed-by-the-weyl-group]](3) a difference on the Grothendieck group implies that the functors are not naturally equivalent; the standard objects generate the Grothendieck group, so it suffices to evaluate on the single object $\Delta(\lambda)$. No claim is made about the existence of a nontrivial natural transformation; the obstruction is already the class.

items.title: Wall-crossing on the projectives in the sl_2 block
items.statement:
Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Work in the regular integral
$\mathfrak{sl}_2$ block with $\lambda=0$, $\rho=1$, so $s\cdot0=-2$ and the
singular wall weight is $\mu=-1$ with $\mu+\rho=0$. The indecomposable
projectives are $P_e=M(0)=\Delta_e$ and $P_s=P(-2)$, whose Verma flag is
$\Delta_e,\Delta_s$ with each standard once
([[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]],
[[lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-the-projective-with-the-top-standard-label]]).

Set $\mathbb k=\mathbb C$.

**On the standards.** By
[[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-standard-modules-by-the-two-step-extension]]
the wall-crossing functor $\theta_s$ of
[[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] satisfies
$\theta_s\Delta_e=\theta_s\Delta_s=P_s$, the nonsplit two-step extension of
$\Delta_s$ by $\Delta_e$: the one-letter reduced word
$w=s$ gives $\theta_s\Delta(\lambda)=P(s\cdot\lambda)$ as its unique new
summand, and the flag computation $\Delta_e+\Delta_s$ shows the summand is the
whole object.

**On the projectives.** Exactness of $\theta_s$
([[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]]) applied
to the flag $0\to\Delta_e\to P_s\to\Delta_s\to0$ shows that $\theta_sP_s$ has
standard flag multiplicities $(\Delta_e,\Delta_s)=(2,2)$. Every projective in
this two-simple block is a direct sum of copies of $P_e$ and $P_s$, whose flag
multiplicities are $(1,0)$ and $(1,1)$ by BGG reciprocity
([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]); writing $\theta_sP_s\cong
P_e^{\oplus a}\oplus P_s^{\oplus b}$, the equations $a+b=2$ and $b=2$ give
$a=0$, $b=2$, so
$$\theta_sP_e\cong P_s,\qquad \theta_sP_s\cong P_s\oplus P_s.$$
In the ordered projective bases $(P_e,P_s)$, with columns indexed by the input,
the matrix of $\theta_s$ is therefore $\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$.
On the Soergel side $C=\mathbb k[x]/(x^2)$ with $\deg x=2$, $C^s=\mathbb k$,
$V(P_e)=\mathbb k$ and $V(P_s)=C$; the wall-crossing theorem
[[thm-wall-crossing-under-the-soergel-functor-is-tensoring-with-the-coinvariant-soergel-bimodule]]
gives
$$V\theta_s(P_e)=C\otimes_{C^s}\mathbb k\cong C,\qquad V\theta_s(P_s)=C\otimes_{C^s}C\cong C\oplus C$$
as left $C$-modules, the left $C$-acting on the first factor, and the
projective Struktursatz
[[thm-soergels-struktursatz-full-faithfulness-on-projectives]] reflects these
isomorphisms back to the projective identities above, all objects involved
being projective.

**Dimension comparison.** The tensor $C\otimes_{C^s}C\cong C\otimes_{\mathbb k}C$
is the four-dimensional coinvariant bimodule $=2|W|$ with $|W|=2$, explicitly
spanned by the four elements $1\otimes1,1\otimes x,x\otimes1,x\otimes x$; the
isomorphism $C\oplus C\to C\otimes_{\mathbb k}C$ of left $C$-modules sends
$(u,v)$ to $u\otimes1+v\otimes x$. By contrast the right-reduced polynomial
$B_s=\mathbb k[a]\otimes_{\mathbb k[a^2]}\mathbb k[a](1)$ is only
two-dimensional, with generator degrees $-1,1$ after centering; the right-reduced polynomial module is $C(1)$, whereas the
coinvariant bimodule $C\otimes_{\mathbb k}C$ has dimension four. The former
models $V\theta_s(P_e)$ and the latter the tensor operator applied to
$V(P_s)=C$.
items.strategy: For the first equality, apply the existing projective-generation and two-step wall-extension lemmas to the one-letter reduced word: theta_s M(0)=P(-2), with standard flag M(0),M(-2). For the second equality, exact biadjoint translation preserves projectives. Apply theta_s to the flag 0→M(0)→P_s→M(-2)→0. Its two outer values are P_s by the existing rank-one two-step extension, so theta_s P_s has standard multiplicities (2,2). Every projective in this two-simple block is a sum of P_e and P_s, whose flags have multiplicities (1,0),(1,1) by BGG reciprocity. The equations a+b=2 and b=2 give a=0,b=2, proving the object isomorphism without treating a class identity as an isomorphism by itself. Alternatively compute with the existing wall-crossing-under-V theorem: s(x)=-x gives C^s=k; the left C-linear isomorphism C⊕C→C⊗_k C sends (u,v) to u⊗1+v⊗x. The projective Struktursatz reflects this isomorphism because all objects concerned are projective. Display both tensor basis and projective multiplicity calculation; no generated B item is a dependency.

items.title: The Soergel functor on the small regular sl_2 block
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers.
Work in the dominant regular integral $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ block at $\lambda=0$,
with $\rho=1$, $W=\{e,s\}$ and $s\cdot0=-2$
([[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]]). Set $\mathbb k=\mathbb C$. Put
$\Delta_e=M(0)$, $\Delta_s=M(-2)=L(-2)$, $P_e=P(0)=\Delta_e$ and $P_s=P(-2)$;
the block is described by the nonsplit sequences
$$0\to L(-2)\to\Delta_e\to L(0)\to0,\qquad 0\to\Delta_e\to P_s\to\Delta_s\to0,$$
the second being the one-letter case of
[[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-standard-modules-by-the-two-step-extension]]
and [[lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-the-projective-with-the-top-standard-label]],
and $P_e=\Delta_e$ being the dominant Verma
([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[def-verma-module]]).

**The values of $V$.** Let $C=\mathbb k[x]/(x^2)$ with $\deg x=2$ be the
coinvariant algebra and $V=\operatorname{Hom}(P_s,-)$
([[def-the-antidominant-projective-and-the-soergel-functor]]), so that
$\operatorname{End}(P_s)\cong C$ by
[[thm-endomorphisms-of-the-antidominant-projective-are-the-coinvariant-algebra]].
Since $P_s$ has indecomposable head $L(-2)$ and $L(-2)=M(-2)$ is simple, the
left $C$-module values are
$$V(P_e)=\mathbb k=C/(x),\quad V(P_s)=C,\quad V(\Delta_e)=V(\Delta_s)=\mathbb k,\quad V(L(0))=0,\quad V(L(-2))=\mathbb k.$$
Indeed $V(\Delta_e)$ and $V(\Delta_s)$ are one-dimensional by exactness applied
to the first sequence and $V(L(-2))=\mathbb k$ from the head quotient, while
$V(L(0))=0$ because $L(0)$ is not a quotient of $P_s$; the unique
one-dimensional $C$-module is $\mathbb k$ with $x$ acting by zero.

**The projective Hom table.** With rows indexed by the source and columns by the
target, the four Hom spaces in the ordered bases $(P_e,P_s)$ are
$$\begin{pmatrix}\operatorname{Hom}(P_e,P_e)&\operatorname{Hom}(P_e,P_s)\\\operatorname{Hom}(P_s,P_e)&\operatorname{Hom}(P_s,P_s)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathbb k&\mathbb k\\\mathbb k&C\end{pmatrix},\qquad\text{dimensions }\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}.$$
Choose the nonzero maps $i\colon P_e\to P_s$ and $p\colon P_s\to P_e$; under the
Struktursatz [[thm-soergels-struktursatz-full-faithfulness-on-projectives]]
their images in $\operatorname{Hom}_C(\mathbb k,C)=\mathbb k\,i_0$ and
$\operatorname{Hom}_C(C,\mathbb k)=\mathbb k\,p_0$ are the generators
$i_0(1)=x$ and $p_0(a+bx)=a$, and the compositions compute
$p_0i_0=0$ on $\mathbb k$ while $i_0p_0=m_x$, multiplication by $x$ on $C$
(equivalently $pi=0$ and $ip$ is a nonzero square-zero
endomorphism; rank one refers to its image under $V$ on $C$). In particular $\operatorname{End}(P_s)\cong C$ is
recovered as the full two-dimensional endomorphism algebra, and the
full-faithfulness comparison is computed on the four projective Hom spaces
rather than claimed for the whole block.

**Polynomial lifts and standard ranks.** For $S=\mathbb k[a]$ with
$s(a)=-a$, the empty-word lift is $B_e=S$ and the rank-one lift is
$$B_s=S\otimes_{\mathbb k[a^2]}S(1)$$
([[def-type-a-soergel-bimodule-for-a-simple-reflection]]); their right origin
reductions are $\mathbb k$ and $C(1)$, whose centered auxiliary degrees are
$-1,1$, and the labels $e^{-1}=e$, $s^{-1}=s$ agree with the dictionary of
[[thm-indecomposable-projectives-correspond-to-indecomposable-soergel-modules]].
Before reduction the standard graph ranks, in the order $(e,s)$, are $(1,0)$
for $B_e$ and $(1,1)$ for $B_s$: in the two-variable model
$B_s=\mathbb k[l,r]/(l^2-r^2)(1)$ the submodule generated by $l-r$ is free of
rank one on the graph $l=-r$ with annihilator $(l+r)$, and the quotient is free of rank one on the graph
$l=r$, with annihilator $(l-r)$
([[def-type-a-standard-graph-bimodules-support-filtrations-and-character]]).
These ranks agree with the Verma-flag multiplicities $(1,0)$ of $P_e$ and
$(1,1)$ of $P_s$ at $v=1$, as predicted by
[[prop-verma-flag-multiplicities-are-standard-filtration-ranks-under-v]]; they
are taken before the graph supports coalesce at the origin, and no grading on
arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects or intrinsic separated-support
filtration on $V(P)$ is asserted.
items.strategy: Use only the named current A-page suppliers and explicit rank-one algebra. In the PBW basis f^n v of M(t), e f^n v=n(t-n+1)f^{n-1}v. At t=0, f v is a singular vector generating M(-2), and the quotient is the one-dimensional L(0); at t=-2 every n>0 coefficient is nonzero, proving simplicity. Highest-weight generation gives nonsplitting of the first sequence. The empty-word case of the projective-generation lemma makes Delta_e=P_e; its one-wall case and the two-step extension lemma give the second sequence and P_s. Since Hom(P_s,L_y) is k for its head y=s and zero for y=e, exactness of V and the displayed composition factors give dimensions 1,2,1,1,0,1 in the stated order. Endomorphismensatz identifies V(P_s) with the regular C-module. The only one-dimensional C-module has x acting by zero, identifying every nonzero dimension-one value with k. Compute Hom_C(k,k)=k, Hom_C(k,C)=kx (annihilator of x), Hom_C(C,k)=k and Hom_C(C,C)=C. Struktursatz with projective targets identifies the four actual O-Hom spaces and compositions; normalize i,p so i(1)=x and p(1)=1, then pi=0 and ip=m_x on the basis 1,x. Independently, the polynomial model for B_s is k[l,r]/(l²-r²)(1). Right reduction r=0 gives k[l]/l²(1). The submodule (l-r) is free rank one on graph l=-r and the quotient is free rank one on graph l=r; the annihilator of l-r is (l+r), since cancellation in k[l,r] is valid. Thus its two standard graph layers have ranks one each. The e lift has only the e graph. Compare the two once-each/one-only Verma flags, invoking the existing multiplicity supplier with total ranks only. The fixed average coordinate in the published two-variable permutation realization is split off and killed on reduction, as explicitly allowed by the existing A-page dictionary. These finite computations illustrate those suppliers, rather than proving their general claims.

items.title: The Soergel functor is not fully faithful on all category-O objects
items.statement:
Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. In the regular integral
$\mathfrak{sl}_2$ block at $\lambda=0$ (so $\rho=1$ and $s\cdot0=-2$), the
functor $V=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P(-2),-)$ is fully faithful on
every object of the block, i.e. $V\colon\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(M,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{C\text{-mod}}(VM,VN)$
is a bijection for all objects $M,N$. This is false.
items.strategy: Compute directly, without relying on another generated B example as a supplier. In the PBW basis, e f^n v=n(t-n+1)f^{n-1}v shows the nonsplit 0→L(-2)→M(0)→L(0)→0 and simplicity of M(-2)=L(-2). P(-2) has unique simple head L(-2), so its Hom to L(0) is zero and its Hom to L(-2) is one dimensional. Exactness of Hom(P(-2),-) then gives V(M(0)) one dimensional; x²=0 makes x act zero on both one-dimensional values. A homomorphism M(0)→L(-2) must send its cyclic highest-weight vector of weight0 to a weight0 vector. The weights of L(-2) are -2,-4,..., so no such vector exists and the Hom is zero. Thus the induced zero→k map is not onto. End(L(0))=k follows directly from its one-dimensional underlying space, giving the independent failure of faithfulness. L(0) is nonprojective since the first nonsplit epimorphism onto it would otherwise split. L(-2) is nonprojective since the nonsplit 0→M(0)→P(-2)→L(-2)→0 from the existing two-step wall extension would otherwise split. State the target-projective hypothesis explicitly; do not replace it by the weaker both-projective wording.
